#1612. Opinion: Liverpool can solve two problems with incredible double transfer

Liverpool have many problems that they need to solve among their ranks.

Andoni Iraola's men are fourth in the Premier League table at the moment with seven points separating them and first-placed Arsenal.

Manchester City and Brighton are the two other teams ahead of them with one point between all three clubs.

Liverpool's rocky start to the season really didn't help matters much and is one of the main reasons why they are where they are right now.

However, with the January transfer window now just around the corner, Liverpool could take advantage of it and force their way back up the table.

Barcelona want to sell Gavi and Alejandro Balde in January

Two of the main positions that the Reds need to upgrade this winter are their left-back and centre-midfield.

Both positions have players among them that haven't met expectations at all this term.

This has led to a lot of underperformance from Liverpool and has forced them to continually experiment with the players that they have at their disposal.

In some cases, players such as Trey Nyoni and Lewis Koumas have massively benefitted from this but, in others, questions remain.

Many different players are on the Reds' shortlist but now, an update from journalist Juan Jesus may have just confirmed who the Reds' main targets could end up being.

"In addition to Alejandro Balde, Barça are now pushing Gavi out this very winter to fund the signing of a centre-back, seen as the club’s absolute priority," he wrote.

"The main target to bolster the defence is Nico Schlotterbeck, but the current wage bill leaves no room to pull off a move of that magnitude in January.

"To comply with financial fair play rules and try to sign him in this winter window, the board is pushing for two key sales: Balde on one hand, and the bombshell departure of Gavi on the other."

Gavi and Alejandro Balde would be two perfect signings for Liverpool

Most Liverpool fans will know that Balde has been linked with the Reds for a while now.

The Spaniard has been left out of Hansi Flick's plans this term with the La Liga giants making it clear since the summer window slammed shut that the 23-year-old had no future left at the Camp Nou.

His natural position is left-back but, he's also been used as a right-back in the past.

Gavi is a completely different kettle of fish altogether. The 22-year-old has played in 179 games throughout his career so far with his best position being a central midfielder.

During his time in Barcelona's first-team squad, he's helped Pedri boss many different midfields and has contributed to 28 goals across all competitions.

Right now, it's unclear how much either of them would cost but, since the Reds' relationship with Barcelona is strong, a deal could definitely be agreed.

#1609. Giving Youri Tielemans a £35m release clause looks like an error... Aston Villa toiling to a draw with Sunderland was more proof Unai Emery could do with a midfield controller in January, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:14 EST, 21 November 2026

Whoever put that £35million release clause in Youri Tielemans’ contract has a heck of a lot to think about these days.

The Belgian midfielder left Aston Villa to join Manchester United last summer and though these are early days in his Old Trafford career, the move does not seem to be working out for anyone.

Unai Emery was distraught to lose Tielemans and against Sunderland, you could see why. Emery signed two central midfielders, Leon Goretzka and Joao Gomes, and has given more minutes to Ross Barkley.

None of the three gives him what Tielemans did and Villa may decide to move for another central player in January. Anything for a bit of cleverness in that part of the pitch.

Tielemans has struggled at United and it will be interesting to see what Mauricio Pochettino makes of him. He is no elite athlete and United supporters and pundits have criticised him because of it but he gave Emery what he craves above all else – control. Neither Gomes nor Goretzka has Tielemans’ passing range and Barkley looks more effective higher up the pitch.

With Sunderland sitting deep here, Villa desperately needed a player who could read the game and create angles like Tielemans. Without him, their passing was slow and predictable, against a Sunderland side without key men Dominic Ballard, Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey.

Sunderland's Nordi Mukiele stretches for the ball but nobody could find the breakthrough

Regis Le Bris saw his side pick up another point to follow their win over Chelsea before the international break - Sunderland now sit 18th

Their only chance in the first half here fell to Emi Buendia, who won the ball high then failed to chip the back-pedalling Robin Roefs. In the second half, Ian Maatsen and substitute Ibrahim Mbaye shot far too close to the Sunderland goalkeeper, who tipped over another effort from Barkley.

Villa have still not lost in the league since they were beaten here by Nottingham Forest in September but teams aiming for the Champions League should put away Sunderland at home. And after 150 Premier League games at the helm, nobody will know that better than Emery.

Buendia reached Aston Villa immortality last May when he scored in the Europa League final and now he has his own banner.

‘It’s Buendia, with a beauty, on the banks of the Bosphorus’ read the slogan in the Holte End.

They will never forget that 3-0 win over Freiburg here but it is alarming just how quickly the team has split apart since then. Six months have passed since Istanbul but only two of the starting XI from that night – Buendia and Torres – were in Unai Emery’s line-up here.

Emi Buendia is now the subject of a banner from Villa fans for his Europa League final heroics

Youri Tielemans scored a stunner in the Europa League final but is now at Man United

True, Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof were injured, while John McGinn was left on the bench, with one eye on Tuesday’s return to Istanbul to face Galatasaray in the Champions League. Boubacar Kamara missed the final through injury.

Still these are huge changes. For most of Emery’s first four years at Villa, every player knew his role and understood the kind of team they were. Now Villa find themselves learning on the job in a three-sided ground, due to the improvement work that leaves the North Stand empty.

Emery knows it too. ‘We have brought a significant number of new players to the squad, many of whom are still adapting to the demands of competing at the level we have worked so hard to establish ourselves at.

ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Wan-Bissaka 6, Harwood-Bellis 6, Torres 7, Maatsen 6; Kamara 6, Goretzka 5 (Barkley 73, 6); Alysson 6, Buendia 6 (McGinn 60, 7), Manzambi 5 (Mbaye 60, 6); Jackson 6 (Madjo 73, 6).

SUNDERLAND (4-2-3-1): Roefs 7; Meunier 7, Mukiele 7, O’Nien 7, Reinildo 7; Ahoka 8, Sadiki 7; Hume 6, Le Fee 7, Talbi 7; Isidor 7 (Angulo 77, 6).

'It takes time, patience, hard work and belief.

‘That is why, now more than ever, we must stick together, trust the direction we are heading in and continue to get behind our players and staff. Results are hugely important but so is recognising the hard work and development that will help us keep moving forward.’

These days clubs like Sunderland cannot afford to wait for young talents to prove themselves in other European leagues.

A decade ago, clubs in the middle of the Premier League could sign players like that for relatively small sums. Now everyone in Europe knows how rich top flight clubs in England are and adjust their prices accordingly.

That is why Sunderland paid nearly £10million for Jules Ahoka even though he had barely played a senior game for Royal Antwerp.

On this evidence, the Black Cats have spent wisely yet again. Ahoka is quick, athletic and strong – exactly what is required in English football today – and his technique is tidy too. If he stays healthy, a bright future awaits.

Ruben Amorim had some interesting comments after the Frosinone win, including why he is not a fan of a term that is going viral.

Milan put on a five-star display at San Siro on Sunday night as they routed that Canarini. All five of their goals came via flowing counter-attacks, which has led to the tag ‘AmorimBall’ doing the rounds on social media, with many believing things are starting to truly click.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The head coach is keeping his feet firmly on the ground though, as he spoke after the game about the need to find consistency both within matches but also from game-to-game. In this sense, Thursday’s trip to face Olympiacos is another big test.

Amorim was present in the press conference room at San Siro following the win to answer questions from journalists, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

“I don’t like that expression. I think we play games to win, we want to dominate the opponent. I don’t think we succeeded today: every game has its own story, and today it was man-on-man.

“Today we didn’t have to prepare much: the idea was simply to give the ball to Pulisic, to Moreira, and then exploit the combinations of these players, the understandings they already have, and conquer space.

“Today you saw that we didn’t spend much time near the opponent’s penalty area and we scored five goals, because the space wasn’t there, it was forty meters away to attack on the run.

“That’s why Cisse came on to play as a striker and not, for example, Camarda: because there was space behind him and Cisse is very good at that. So, I think we’ve played very good games in the past, but today it was just a question of the quality of the players, of one-on-ones, of reading the game.

“Today it wasn’t a question of the coach, I think, but of the players. And they, since it was man-on-man, just had to do what they can do. when they’re so good: beating the man and opening up space. So today the credit goes entirely to the players.”

“I watched the France game and I think he’s one of the best players on the team. So I think his importance is paramount. You can see there’s rotation, there’s a lot of talent. France has a lot of talent, but Rabiot is always there. There’s a reason for that.

“And then, if you look at the way France play, with Mbappé, with the way all these players position themselves on the pitch, sometimes with four players with Olise as the No. 10, he has to stay there to play a different kind of game.

“With us, he’s the player who has to push the team forward, he’s the decisive element. In France, however, he has a different job to do. So it depends more on his role in the national team and his role at Milan.

“This changes his way of interpreting the game, and it’s further proof of how Rabiot can play by adapting to the team he’s in. For me, therefore, he’s one of the best midfielders in Europe. I hope his contract renewal comes soon.”

“Today’s match wasn’t just about tactics. We saw changes in position, one-on-one situations with plenty of space: it seemed like a crazy game. What I felt against Genoa and in the other matches was that we were too far away, we didn’t reach the final third of the pitch.

“We’re not like the big teams: if you look at the big teams, like Juventus, they might struggle to get results, but you see the volume they produce. For us, it’s a bit of the opposite, so I’m really worried that, if we don’t improve, we won’t be able to maintain this number of points.

“Today, however, was a step forward: we saw many players attacking the depth, something we hadn’t seen against Ferencvaros. In the other matches, we’d managed the ball well, but today we needed pace and runs.

“We need to be able to play both games within the same game, but today was clearly the type of game we needed to win.”

#1606. Brentford transfer news: Bees among three Premier League clubs keen on '£33m-rated' Serie A star

By Ben Sully | 25 Nov 2026 00:26, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 02:43

Brentford are reportedly among three Premier League clubs interested in signing Lazio midfielder Kenneth Taylor.

The Bees splashed out around £41m to recruit midfielder Mamadou Sangare from Lens in the summer in a club-record transfer.

Sangare has featured in all 11 of Brentford's Premier League games, but he has not always been a guaranteed starter due to the competition from Vitaly Janelt and Yehor Yarmoliuk.

Mathias Jensen is also available to Brentford boss Keith Andrews, who currently has plenty of options at his disposal in central midfield.

However, Jensen is out of contract at the end of the season, and the uncertainty surrounding his future may be one of the factors behind Brentford's apparent interest in Taylor.

According to TuttoMercatoWeb, the Bees are one of three Premier League clubs that are keeping tabs on the Dutchman's performances at Lazio.

Bournemouth and Newcastle United are also showing a keen interest as they scour the market for potential midfield recruits.

The Cherries are believed to view Taylor as a potential replacement for Alex Scott, who continues to draw interest from some of the Premier League's biggest clubs.

Meanwhile, Newcastle appear to be still open to bolstering a midfield that lost the services of Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali at the end of last season, despite recruiting Nico Gonzalez and Aladji Bamba in the summer window.

Taylor has played regularly since joining Lazio from Ajax in January, contributing five goals and five assists in 34 competitive appearances.

In fact, he has registered two goals and three assists in 12 league matches this term, helping Gennaro Gattuso's side establish a two-point lead at the top of Serie A.

With Taylor under contract until June 2030, there is a belief his potential suitors will have to offer around €40m (£33m) to have any hope of prising him away from Lazio.

However, a January departure seems unlikely at this stage, with Gattuso keen to keep one of his key players for the club's title battle.

Brentford, Bournemouth and Newcastle will also have to be wary of rival interest from Juventus, who view him as the 'ideal' midfield target.

#1605. Man City are failing to give their supporters something to stand behind as Enzo Maresca's side radiate uncertainty with meek display in Fulham draw, writes JACK GAUGHAN

Published: 11:04 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:16 EST, 21 November 2026

The bananas are disappearing now winter is coming, the fire and fury waning with each passing week. In legal limbo, Manchester City’s supporters need something – anything – to stand behind but increasingly their team refuse to provide that solace.

City were booed off at the end as Enzo Maresca ducked down the tunnel. Some of that could have been directed at referee Thomas Bramall, after Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal, but certainly a significant number were jeering what they’d just seen. That simply does not happen at the Etihad Stadium, even during the torrid run of two years ago.

But they are witnessing a squad who radiate uncertainty. Who take three touches when two will do; who always receive possession squarely facing their own goal; who do not create passing lines for their mates. And crucially, who are forever momentarily confused as to who exactly is picking up which runner and those split seconds make all the difference in this division.

There is just this strange state of unease around how they want to approach games at the moment, something that adversity can provoke and something that Maresca is adamant he can correct. A coach of his calibre should do given the time and freedom.

Yet when he spent the two-week international break studying clips and fashioning ways of improving, he cannot have envisaged a scenario whereby home fans were so incredulous at a lack of energy that they were roused to their feet when Haaland deigned to close down Bernd Leno and force an error.

Man City put in an underwhelming performance as they were held to a 1-1 draw by Fulham

Enzo Maresca's side are radiating uncertainty and look worryingly vulnerable at the back

Rodrigo Muniz made City pay as he put an impressive Fulham 1-0 ahead after 16 minutes

Fulham popped it about nicely and at will. Found pockets to hurt their illustrious hosts, who were again asking a centre half – in this case Marc Guehi – to charge into midfield. City did have more balance than at Nottingham Forest for including Ayyoub Bouaddi for Enzo Fernandez, yet Alvaro Arbeloa still aggressively pressed them in that area to some success.

‘I told the players that we will have the chance to beat them if we play with courage,’ said Arbeloa, who was indebted to the towering performance of defender David Affengruber.

Arsenal will have watched this grinning and could easily be racking up an unassailable lead once these teams meet in north London next Sunday. Unassailable with all the usual caveats about the appeal and what this season may or may not eventually mean.

City did create enough statistically but as with other games of late, that did not tell the whole story.

Calvin Bassey pirouetted through midfield, the heavily derided Gianluigi Donnarumma thwarting a number of strong Fulham chances, and City appeared somewhat lost and out of ideas.

Elliot Anderson equalised with a superb volley but City failed to create much after that

Maresca expressed his concern at City's lack of clean sheets after they struggled again

That is a worrying departure from recent defeats, where they attacked with the same abandon as that early season flourish when they might as well have hosted games at Madison Square Gardens and played with an orange ball.

MAN CITY (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 7; Khusanov 6, Dias 6, Guehi 5, O’Reilly 5 (Gvardiol 78); Anderson 7, Bouaddi 7 (Fernandez 85); Ndiaye 6 (Allan 78), Foden 7 (Cherki 70), Doku 5; Haaland 5

FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Leno 6; Tete 6, Affengruber 8, Bassey 7, Sessegnon 7 (Palacios 83); Berge 6, Charles 7; Bobb 7 (Garcia 78), King 6 (Larsson 70, 6), Iwobi 7 (Robinson 70, 6); Muniz 7 (Cairney 83)

Met with a Fulham who had not conceded more than once in the league since the start of September, City failed to create a meaningful opportunity in the last 25 minutes of a match they were desperate to win and should have been in the ascendancy of after Elliot Anderson’s volleyed equaliser after half time.

Maresca, though, is more concerned with a lack of clean sheets. It’s now none of those in nine games in all competitions for the first time in seven years, with Rodrigo Muniz opening the scoring on 16 minutes. A throw inside Fulham’s own third prompted Guehi to jump and lose his duel, City turned around and Oscar Bobb laid on for Muniz.

‘We’re conceding too many goals,’ Maresca said. ‘We need to avoid it. You need to win games 1-0. You need clean sheets. We’re not able to do it. But I can see many positive aspects. We started four months ago and not four years ago.

‘We’ve conceded almost 80 per cent of our goals at the start of the first half and second half. It’s something we need to improve. It’s a throw in at the corner flag and nobody is expecting they can create something.’

Maresca was also insistent that Haaland ought to have been awarded an equaliser before the break when poking in on the goal line, yet Bramall adjudged that Leno had the ball under control on field, with VAR not overruling.

Some hard luck, some profligacy with Haaland squandering a couple of big chances, but the day was summed up when in stoppage time, Jeremy Doku was penalised for a foul throw.

Rio Ngumoha was always destined to be a superstar, and he is continuing his excellent development at Anfield this season.

The 18-year-old has appeared in all but two games for the Reds this campaign, making eight starts and recently giving Andoni Iraola a genuine selection headache.

Sunday's demolition of Manchester United was a breakout moment for the teenager and was a clear message to the coaching staff in L4 that Rio is ready to start every game for Liverpool going forward.

Rio Ngumoha is a real superstarThere are few bigger games for Liverpool than clashes against Manchester United, and Ngumoha leaving his mark on Sunday's win will be remembered as a key moment in the youngster's rise. #1603. Doncaster Rovers vs Huddersfield Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 25 Nov 2026 01:26

Doncaster Rovers will welcome Huddersfield Town to Club Doncaster Sports Village on Thursday for a Yorkshire Derby with importance at both ends of the League One table.

The visitors fell off the summit of the division following a defeat at the weekend, while their hosts drew on Saturday and only lead the relegation zone on goal difference.

Doncaster Rovers head back into action on Thursday aiming to move clear of the relegation zone at the beginning of the League One weekend, having endured a difficult start to the campaign.

In their second season back in the third tier after promotion from League Two and a 14th-placed finish last time around, the Yorkshire outfit currently find themselves 20th having managed just 13 points from their first 14 outings, losing seven and winning just three of those.

Indeed, their last six outings have produced just four points, as Grant McCann's side broke up four defeats with a 2-0 home victory over Sheffield Wednesday, before falling to Luton Town and MK Dons away from home and experiencing mixed fortunes in a pair of cup ties against Rochdale and Kidderminster Harriers, losing to the latter in the FA Cup first round.

A trip to Yorkshire rivals Bradford City followed on Saturday, and the Rovers were at least able to bounce back from consecutive league defeats, twice falling behind and levelling through Jordan Thomas in the 78th minute and Sean Grehan deep into injury time to leave with a creditable point from a 2-2 draw.

Still only leading the bottom four on goal difference, Doncaster Rovers will now aim to bounce back to winning ways to put themselves three points above the drop zone before the rest of the weekend's action.

They face a tough test, though, as the visitors arrive in search of a rebound of their own to return to the top of the table.

Beginning their third straight season in League One and their first full one under the management of Martin Drury with the hopes of battling for promotion back to the second tier, Huddersfield Town have enjoyed a strong start as they headed into the November international break in top spot on 29 points from 14 games.

The Terriers won eight and only lost one of those while scoring 28 goals and conceding just 12, having headed into that break in a seven-game league unbeaten run in which they won four in a row before drawing against fellow promotion-chasers Luton Town in early November.

Then following a brief international break and a pair of cup outings against Exeter City and Liverpool Under-21s, Drury's side returned at home to Leicester City on Saturday but fell to just a second loss of the season in the third tier as Louis Page scored the only goal of the game for the visitors early in the second half.

That saw Huddersfield Town fall three points behind new leaders Stockport County, albeit with a game in hand, but only ahead of third-placed Oxford United having played a game more, and they will hope to quickly put things right and retake their place at the summit with a Yorkshire derby win on Thursday.

Doncaster Rovers form (all competitions):

Huddersfield Town form (all competitions):

Doncaster Rovers remain without James Husband, Tommi O'Reilly and Francis Okoronkwo due to ongoing injuries, while Harry Clifton and Will Keane missed the game against Bradford and will likely remain sidelined too.

Brandon Hanlan led the line in that game and may continue to do so with Alfie May ineligible against his parent club, although James Collins is back in contention having made his Rovers league debut off the bench at the weekend following a long layoff.

Elsewhere, George Broadbent should again join Robbie Gotts and mainstay Owen Bailey in midfield.

Huddersfield Town are still without Murray Wallace, Jack Whatmough, David Kasumu, Herbie Kane and Marcus McGuane through injuries.

Drury should avoid making many changes despite the weekend's defeat, with Radinio Balker, Ibane Bowat and Sean Roughan having formed a strong back three in recent weeks and Cameron Humphreys and Archie Collins likely to continue their midfield partnership.

Joe Taylor and Derensili Sanches Fernandes have shone in attack, with the former scoring 10 goals in 14 league games and the latter notching up seven goals and six assists in 15.

Doncaster Rovers possible starting lineup:

Simkin; Nixon, Grehan, Pearson, Senior; Broadbent, Gotts; Hutchinson, Bailey, Thomas; Hanlan

Huddersfield Town possible starting lineup:

Huddersfield Town will hope their rare defeat at the weekend does not derail their promotion push, and despite the hosts taking a point from Bradford at the weekend, we back the Terriers to bounce back on Thursday and outclass Doncaster.

#1602. No advantage played and an indirect free-kick: Pairetto criticised for Milan-Frosinone officiating

Referee Luca Pairetto has been criticised for his performance in AC Milan’s 5-1 win over Frosinone last night.

This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) comments on three incidents above all in which the referee ultimately seemed incapable of providing the right decision, one of which could have cost a goal.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the first half, Adrien Rabiot stole the ball from Cittadini, who blatantly dragged him back by the shirt. The ball rolled to Goncalo Ramos who was through on goal and had a man to his left, effectively making it a two-on-zero break with just the goalkeeper to beat.

Yet, the referee Pairetto blew his whistle for a foul and showed a yellow card to the defender. He immediately apologised for his error in failing to play the clear advantage for the Rossoneri, in an incident reminiscent of the Junior Messias goal not given against Spezia in 2021-22.

That wasn’t all, either. Nine minutes into the second half, an indirect free-kick was awarded inside the Frosinone penalty area following a clear back-pass from Calvani to Palmisani, that was actually flagged by the assistant referee and not initially given by Pairetto.

Former referee Mauro Bergonzi commented on the refereeing incidents in Milan-Frosinone to La Domenica Sportiva.

“In the first half, the referee failed to take the lead: he missed the lead, he squandered it, if we’re being honest. The situation is this: Cittadini fouls Rabiot, who steals the ball, a clear hold, the referee hastily calls the foul, and he also realises it immediately because he stops, as if to say, ‘Wow, it’s a shame I called’ because Gonçalo Ramos was hurtling toward goal.

“He apologizes, he says: ‘No, I apologise, I’m booking the Frosinone player.’ He said sorry. But this is something that really bothers you from a refereeing perspective because the lead was clear, but the referee’s gesture is commendable because he raises his hands and humbly says: ‘I made a mistake’.

“53rd minute: we rarely see them called on football pitches during matches. It’s a deliberate back pass from Calvani to the goalkeeper, the goalkeeper saves it, the referee wouldn’t have called anything, he turns to the right, looks at the assistant because the assistant signals it to him.

“Pairetto tells the assistant, ‘Well done’ and, to make matters worse, ‘Well done’ again. The assistant was good because he saw it perfectly correctly. He made his choice, he got it right because this is a pass, a deliberate back pass.

“Chiffi, the fourth official, is also there, pressing the button to communicate with the refereeing team via his headset, and if the assistant hadn’t seen it, the fourth official would have signaled it.”

#1601. VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

The big moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

On this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams said: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”

Glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” said Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision.  We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”

While Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

One of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi said: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something important.

“If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with big qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi said: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”

After the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

It’s full time at GTech Stadium: Brentford 1 Sunderland 1

City needed Donnarumma to spare their blushes with several good saves.

Erling Haaland at the back post with a thunderous header – his 300th goal in club football.

The big headline news from Tottenham is that Mykhailo Mudryk is on the bench.

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi plans to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

#1600. Jude Bellingham dismisses Ballon d'Or talk after scoring "best goal of my life" against PSV Eindhoven

By Seye Omidiora | 25 Nov 2026 01:48, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 01:51

Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham has brushed off Ballon d'Or talk after inspiring his side to a commanding 5-1 Champions League comeback victory over PSV Eindhoven.

The 23-year-old England international started Tuesday's league phase encounter at the Santiago Bernabeu on the bench as Jose Mourinho opted to manage his workload following recent fatigue.

With Los Blancos trailing 1-0 at the interval to an Ivan Perisic penalty, Mourinho summoned Bellingham at half-time and the substitute immediately transformed the contest.

After Federico Valverde restored parity five minutes into the second period, Bellingham put the hosts ahead on the hour mark with a sensational strike before later setting up Vinicius Junior's late fifth.

Bellingham's decisive go-ahead strike immediately drew comparisons to club icon Zinedine Zidane, whose famous number five shirt the Englishman wears in the Spanish capital.

Collecting the ball on the edge of the penalty area, the midfielder flicked it up with his first touch before slicing an audacious outside-of-the-boot volley inside the far post.

Speaking after the final whistle, Bellingham admitted the acrobatic effort stood above anything else he has produced in his career so far.

"I think this was the best goal of my life," Bellingham said, as reported by Fabrizio Romano.

@FabrizioRomano That was a prefect goal https://t.co/4j8kLOdUMX

Teammate Bernardo Silva echoed the widespread awe inside the stadium, describing the strike as "one of those moments when you just go, 'Wow!'"

Bellingham's dazzling second-half appearance prompted Mourinho to reiterate his belief that omitting the midfielder from the top 10 at this year's Ballon d'Or ceremony was jarring.

The Portuguese tactician also conceded that leaving his talisman out of the starting lineup had backfired, admitting he had mistakenly believed Madrid could win without him.

When pressed on the prestigious individual accolade afterwards, however, Bellingham made it clear that collective silverware remains his sole obsession.

"Ballon d'Or? I do not care," he declared. "It's for journalists, not for me. I want to win all titles with Real Madrid."

Having helped Los Blancos preserve their 100% start in the Champions League league phase, Bellingham will now look to carry his sparkling form back into La Liga action this weekend.

Mourinho's team are three points off Barcelona in the La Liga table ahead of their next match against Alaves.

#1599. Opinion: Liverpool need to compete for the next Virgil van Dijk

Liverpool have earned a reputation for recruiting some of the best young players in world football in recent seasons.

The additions of Rio Ngumoha, Trey Nyoni and more recently Jeremy Jacquet and Luca Brughmans are proof of the philosophy in place within Liverpool's recruitment team.

With Julian Ward at the helm, the recruitment strategy doesn't seem to have changed, and the Reds continue to be linked with some of the most promising young talents from across Europe and beyond.

Liverpool's mission remains the same but that doesn't mean that they are automatically the favourites for every wonderkid, and they appear to be falling behind in the race for one highly rated defender.

Liverpool behind in race for next Van DijkRuud Nijstad is quickly becoming one of the most exciting prospects in the Eredivisie, and the Dutch U19 international is earning himself plenty of attention. The 18-year-old has started all but one game for FC Twente in the league this season, and has established himself as a central part of John van den Brom's side. Standing at 6'5, Nijstad already holds the stature of a Premier League defender, and his impressive performances for Twente, both domestically and in the UEFA Conference League, have led to interest from several top sides.

Ruud Nijstad is quickly becoming one of the most exciting prospects in the Eredivisie, and the Dutch U19 international is earning himself plenty of attention.

The 18-year-old has started all but one game for FC Twente in the league this season, and has established himself as a central part of John van den Brom's side.

Standing at 6'5, Nijstad already holds the stature of a Premier League defender, and his impressive performances for Twente, both domestically and in the UEFA Conference League, have led to interest from several top sides.

A report from Ekrem Konur recently named Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Chelsea and Manchester United as the four clubs with the most advanced interest, and it appears that Liverpool are already falling behind in the race for the next Dutch colossus.

Nijstad is also capable of playing at left-back and is left-footed, making him an ideal long-term replacement for Virgil van Dijk.

Having the chance to learn from the man who captain's his national team could be vital for Nijstad, who could command a fee of over €30 million (~£25m) according to Konur.

Liverpool clearly aren't leading the race for Nijstad, but he would be an excellent January pick up and Ward & Co should definitely be taking a look at the 18-year-old.

#1598. Formidable and relentless Bournemouth's astonishing form is no mere hot streak, writes JAMES SHARPE, as dominant Cherries beat Forest to claim NINTH win in a row

Published: 12:38 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:28 EST, 21 November 2026

This is all becoming rather inevitable at Bournemouth. Will they ever stop winning? Will Evanilson ever stop scoring?

The numbers alone are astonishing. Nine wins on the bounce for the first time in their history, their victory here against Nottingham Forest making it six on the spin at home at an aggregate score of 15 to nil. Five wins in a row in the Premier League for the first time, too, a result that moved them into the top four.

This is Bournemouth, remember. Only this is Bournemouth now.

Make no mistake: this is no hot streak. This is not a team under Marco Rose carried to win after win after win on a wave of momentum and vibes. This is relentless, breathtaking stuff. This is a team that, week after week, outplays every team that stands in front of them. It doesn’t matter if it’s Forest, or Manchester United, or AC Milan. Bournemouth turn up and they blow their opponents away.

They move it quicker and sharper, they win it back faster and higher. They give teams no time to think or breathe, so it’s little wonder they have no answer.

‘We never really struggled, said Rose. 'We suffered a little bit at the end, but we defended quite well together, and that's why it's a deserved win.

Bournemouth racked up their sixth successive league victory and ninth in all competitions

'If we use the right approach every game – and this is really, really demanding – we win games. Next game, we have to prove it again. If we do it, then we can keep the level up. But as I said, this is a tough job.

‘The collective is strong, but even this we have to maintain. Because if you win games…I mean, some of our players right now are in a lot of noise and rumours.

'If we are able to keep these kinds of things away from the locker room, and if everyone comes into training every day, works hard and gives everything for the club and the team, then we are really, really good.'

The only real surprise was that Evanilson, Bournemouth’s talismanic Brazilian, didn’t leave with more than just his one, now customary, goal.

That itself was another fine finish after Tyler Adams won the ball high up the pitch – obviously – dinked it across to James Hill, back after his first England call-up, who flicked a header into Evanilson’s path. He thumped it past Matz Sels to do the rest.

Rose, who called him a ‘real No9’ the other week, had been urging him to get into the box more to finish off chances. He did that, all right. Twice earlier in the game, he raced on to through balls only to be denied by Sels and a last-ditch tackle from Jair Cunha.

His opening strike, his eighth goal in his last nine games, means he is the first Premier League player to reach double figures for goal contributions with six goals alongside his four other assists. He leads the press, he creates chances, he scores goals. He does the lot.

That’s now six league games in a row he’s found the net, halfway to breaking Jamie Vardy’s record of 11 in a row. You wouldn’t put it past him.

Bournemouth’s talismanic Brazilian Evanilson scored for the sixth successive league match

Forest came into this, after all, off the back of a huge, much-needed victory against Manchester City. After just one win in Oliver Glasner’s opening nine league games, that was the performance those around Forest felt that could spark the season into life.

It was also meant to be the one where Liam Delap’s Forest career burst into life with two thunderous goals in a bullying, battering-ram showing.

Alas, they both ran into a proper team this week.

Forest tried to go direct to Delap, partly to try to bypass the intense Bournemouth press, but nothing stuck. Delap lost possession with 23 of his 39 touches. He committed more fouls than he had shots and found his way into the referee’s book for clumsily bundling over Adam Smith.

The visitors huffed and puffed in the second half but never really looked like scoring. The closest they got was a couple of speculative long-range efforts from Morgan Gibbs-White and James McAtee before a late goalmouth scramble nearly provided an opening through chaos more than creativity.

It was only the busy hands of Sels that kept the scoring respectable.

’The defeat was deserved,’ said Glasner. ‘City and today were completely different. It's like a different sport. This is football, but it's different.

'When teams play like City, when it's more of a tactical game, we are doing well. When it's more of a physical, intense game, we're struggling. Today our weaknesses came to the surface.’

When asked if he had the players to play this way, Glasner responded: 'Right now, I have to say no. If not, we will add players. If we believe we need somebody to add this physicality, these quick solutions, we will do it.'

Did they expect much else, though? Forest never beat Bournemouth. That’s 13 meetings in a row now they have failed to win.

‘Nottingham Forest, it’s happened again,’ sang the home fans in the final few minutes.

Liam Delap and Nottingham Forest crashed into a proper team as they came back down to earth after their win over Man City before the international break

Marcus Tavernier's performances could get a chance with England if he maintains his form

Bournemouth have already had a couple of deserved England call-ups this season in Hill and midfielder Alex Scott. How long until Marcus Tavernier gets his chance?

No English player has scored more Premier League goals this season than the Bournemouth winger, level with Morgan Rogers and Dominic Calvert-Lewin, and once again he was at the heart of everything good the Cherries do.

His superb cross behind the Forest defence found Justin Kluivert for Bournemouth’s second of the afternoon. He danced through the Forest defence to set up Rayan for a late chance.

'It was my 11th Premier League game today, and I couldn't see better offensive midfielders so far this season,’ said Rose.

‘If you see how he works and how he plays, the quality he has, he scores goals. He's 27, he's at the best age.

‘If he plays well, if he stays healthy, I think, like with Hilly, these things come. They're just around the corner.'

#1597. Ramos upset by substitution: The clarification and why Cisse came on over Camarda

Goncalo Ramos got his name on the scoresheet in AC Milan’s rout of Frosinone, but he was forced off in the second half.

As Sky (via Calciomercato.com) report, everything seemed great when Milan were dominating Frosinone at San Siro and scoring nearly every time they went forward. However, during the second half, a minor alarm sounded.

Ruben Amorim was forced to replace his Ramos in the 50th minute. The Portuguese striker – who had scored in the first half – was hastily removed from the pitch by the head coach shortly after Ardon Jashari’s goal to make it 3-1.

The reason? The change was made due to a minor muscle problem that the player reported to the bench, even though Ramos himself did not seem happy about the substitution at the time of the change.

The former PSG man informed the bench that he had a small calf problem and – to avoid worsening the issue – Amorim immediately opted for a substitution. Alphadjo Cisse was sent on in his place, and he scored the fourth goal just a few minutes later.

When he was taken off, Ramos showed a grimace of disapproval towards his bench, miming the ‘wait’ gesture. He then complained that he would have liked to try to stay on the pitch, but some post-match comments cleared things up.

When asked if his calf is ok, he told DAZN: “Yes, yes, everything’s fine, everything’s fine.” Rabiot later revealed the background to the substitution to Sky, admitting that he played a hand in convincing the coach.

“Gonçalo is the first player to do a lot. Today I saw he had a bit of pain in his thigh. I know he’s a very important player for us, and we have a lot of matches. I even asked the coach to let him rest a bit,” the Frenchman said.

Speaking to DAZN after the final whistle, Amorim was asked why he felt it was right for Cisse to come on rather than Francesco Camarda, the only other natural centre-forward in the squad

“We didn’t spend many minutes near the penalty area; he was behind. Today we were 40 metres from the goal, and Cisse was perfect for that. That’s why I didn’t bring on Camarda for Ramos: I needed someone who could run in behind.”

#1596. Rodrigo Bentancur transfer: Aston Villa 'pursuit' of £8.4m-valued player could 'trigger' Tottenham Hotspur exit

By Seye Omidiora | 25 Nov 2026 02:12

Argentine giants Boca Juniors are reportedly keen to bring Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Rodrigo Bentancur back to Buenos Aires as they prepare for next year's Copa Libertadores.

While funding a deal for the 29-year-old Uruguay international would normally prove difficult, the potential sale of highly rated youngster Milton Delgado could hand Boca the financial firepower required.

Aston Villa are among a host of English clubs tracking the 21-year-old defensive midfielder, meaning a winter raid from Unai Emery's side could directly threaten Tottenham's midfield depth.

According to Argentine outlets El Crack Deportivo and El Intransigente via Sport Witness, Boca president Juan Roman Riquelme has already started preliminary work on re-signing Bentancur.

Riquelme views the Spurs stalwart as his preferred candidate to replace Delgado should the academy graduate depart La Bombonera in the coming months.

Bentancur progressed through Boca's youth ranks before earning a switch to Juventus in 2017 and is seen as the ideal experienced presence to anchor their upcoming continental campaign.

The South American outfit plan to reinvest the proceeds from Delgado's prospective transfer straight into a formal approach for their former player.

Delgado's stock has risen even further after he played the full 90 minutes in Boca's 2-0 Copa Sudamericana final triumph over Atletico Mineiro on Saturday.

Villa are reportedly preparing a formal January offer for Delgado after scouting the 21-year-old extensively across the past six months.

However, Emery's side are far from alone in the race, with Chelsea, Bournemouth, Brighton and West Ham United all linked with the youngster.

Boca are believed to have previously rejected a £7.5m bid from MLS side Atlanta United back in August, around the same time Chelsea and Bournemouth lodged initial enquiries for the young midfielder, who is valued at €10m (£8.4m) by Transfermarkt.

Portuguese outfit Porto are also believed to be monitoring developments from Europe, leaving Riquelme in a strong position to command a substantial fee if a bidding war erupts.

Even if Boca secure the necessary funds, convincing Bentancur to leave North London could prove complicated given that he signed a new long-term contract with Tottenham in October 2025 and has spent almost a decade competing at the top level in Europe.

#1595. Report: Andoni Iraola eyes deal for new long-term Liverpool target

Julian Ward and Andoni Iraola have a lot of work to do on Liverpool's first-team squad this January.

Over £150 million was already spent on the club this summer but, since they're currently fourth in the table and find themselves seven points adrift of first-placed Arsenal, they have a bit of ground to make up.

Obviously, all of their problems can't be rectified in the winter window but, if they can fix some of their main ones, that would be spectacular.

Not only would bringing in another player or two give the Reds a boost but, it would also help them get back on track and start to get back to their best.

Liverpool see Gustavo Varela as a 'long-term target' rather than a short-term option

Over the last few days, the transfer rumour mill has been going into overdrive.

Every single position among the Reds ranks is being scrutinised with fans seemingly rather happy with the recent performances of their club.

On Sunday, they managed to beat Manchester United 4-0 and, even though the Red Devils were down to 10 men for most of the day, Liverpool's performance was still impressive.

However, their problem areas were made clear once again with only two strikers available for Iraola to choose from.

And, of the two, one of them was Lewis Koumas who, even though he's good, he doesn't really jump out as a Premier League-winning attacker.

Because of this, rumours about the future of Liverpool's attack have emerged with Monza's Gustavo Varela now appearing on the Reds' shortlist.

However, a recent report from Football Insider has clarified just how serious Liverpool are about bringing the Portuguese striker in.

"Liverpool will not prioritise a move to sign Monza striker Gustavo Varela in January, sources have told Football Insider," they wrote.

"The 21-year-old has emerged as a target for the Reds, having struck 11 goals from his opening 11 games in Serie A so far this term.

"The Reds are "keeping tabs" on the Portuguese youngster, with several top Italian clubs also having their "eyes fixed on him" at the moment.

"However, sources say that Varela is viewed as more of a long-term option at Anfield, and the club are not likely to make a move for him this winter.

"Monza are relaxed over their frontman's future for now, but they know that further interest from top clubs is inevitable if he continues to perform."

Gustavo Varela is an interesting transfer for Liverpool to explore

Varela is almost certainly a player that barely anyone outside of Italy will have heard of.

The Portuguese striker is the Serie A's current top goal scorer despite his team being in a relegation battle.

The strangest thing is that, he only just joined the Italian outfit during the 2026-27 summer transfer window for €2.5 million.

Before this term, he'd had a couple of poor seasons but now, he really seems to have come into his own despite only being 21 years old.

His age coupled with his keen eye for goal are two major boxes that Liverpool like to tick when looking for attackers and, if the fee that Monza want is reasonable, there's no reason why a deal couldn't be explored.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Some have questioned if the Canarini were a bit too aggressive in their approach to the game, given they played with such a high line and allowed space for Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to exploit.

Alvini was present in the press conference room at San Siro after the full-time whistle and he analysed what was perhaps the most difficult night of the season for his team. MilanNews transcribed his assessments.

Should the game have been played differently?

“Frosinone played their game but made a few mistakes they don’t usually make, but that’s certainly not my concern, losing by such a large margin. What’s worrying are the mistakes we made that we could have avoided.”

“We made a mistake on the first goal, which was a mistake of our own, while the other goals we conceded were goals we absolutely could have avoided. We conceded them and were naive.

“It’s a mistake of our own, and so today, from this perspective, if you come to Milan against Milan and make these mistakes, it’s only natural that we end up losing like this, by such a large scoreline.

“That’s the analysis, even though I think the scoreline is even too large: the first half, in my opinion, was extraordinary on our part.”

Did the absences have an impact, forcing you to experiment a bit?

“There’s nothing experimental about it. We played with the same principles, running forward to get to Rabiot. We preferred to bring on a defender who would push forward rather than a midfielder.

“In my opinion, this definitely didn’t influence the result, but rather the attitude, the idea, or the match strategy. And we certainly made – as I said before and I’ll repeat – mistakes we don’t usually make.

“If you give Milan certain chances, with such strong players and the quality of this team, you risk losing, and that’s what happened. You risk losing with a heavy defeat, and that’s what happened.

“He had a problem with that back heel in the box, and he definitely needs tests. It’s too early now; we’ll have to wait for the tests, which will be done starting Tuesday, but it’s definitely a problem.”

“We had a chance with Monterisi after a minute, we hit the post, and we created a lot. I have nothing to say to the team for their attitude and the way they played.

“We, I repeat, made some naivety, some mistakes. It’s also up to me to understand that there are important players on the other side who can cause problems.”

“It’s a result that definitely needs to be managed, navigated, and channeled, but it doesn’t change my attitude at all. We have 20 points today. The path we need to take is to try to stay in Serie A, and we’ll try to do so with this attitude, with this identity: this is the path we’ll take.

“Four years ago, I drew a game against Milan by playing defensively, and we took home a point. Today we made some mistakes, but this is the path we’ll take. I’m happier with the management, with the team’s identity, to try to achieve that objective, and this is what we’ll continue to do.”

By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 07:10

Real Madrid produced a sensational second-half comeback to beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday evening, with England star Jude Bellingham proving instrumental after being introduced at half-time.

Jose Mourinho's side were trailing 1-0 at the interval following Ivan Perisic's penalty, but Federico Valverde restored parity before the 23-year-old produced a spectacular volley to put Los Blancos ahead. Kylian Mbappe scored twice, and Vinicius Junior added a fifth to complete the turnaround.

AS were particularly impressed, publishing the headline "Bellingham: lo cambio todo" - 'Bellingham changed everything'.

Manu de Juan highlighted how the England international reorganised Madrid's midfield, allowing Arda Guler to operate deeper and giving the hosts greater control and attacking momentum. AS also praised his spectacular volley for the 2-1 lead and his subsequent assist for Vinicius.

El Pais delivered perhaps the most glowing assessment, publishing the headline "El esplendor deslumbrante de Bellingham impulsa la goleada del Madrid al PSV" - Bellingham's 'dazzling brilliance' drives Madrid's thrashing of PSV.

Mourinho also described Bellingham as a different type of player who provided something Madrid had been missing during the opening 45 minutes.

The statistics underline why the praise was justified. Despite playing just 45 minutes, Bellingham registered one goal, one assist and created three chances. According to Sofascore, he also completed 100% of his attempted dribbles, won all of his tackles and claimed 75% of his duels.

His influence extended beyond the spectacular finish, with his movement between the lines helping Madrid establish control and create opportunities for their forwards.

There is little doubt that Bellingham was the defining figure in Madrid's comeback - while Mourinho's triple half-time substitution and improved collective pressing also played important roles, the Englishman's ability to bring structure, energy and creativity to the midfield was particularly striking.

Receiving such glowing praise from the Spanish media and his manager after just 45 minutes illustrates the level Bellingham can reach when operating at his best. #1585. Transfer news: Major Saudi Pro League rule change could shake up the market

By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 07:26

With a little over a month to go until the transfer window reopens, clubs around the world are already moving behind the scenes to strengthen their squads. Saudi Arabia, which has become a leading player in the market in recent years, is considering a change that could boost its domestic league but worry other countries.

According to The Times, the Saudi Pro League (SPL) is considering raising the limit on foreign players ahead of the 2027-28 window, which could trigger a new wave of signings. Saudi clubs are seeking clarification on the matter before the Northern Hemisphere winter window in January.

At present, clubs in Saudi Arabia can register up to eight foreign players in a 25-man squad, with the option of adding two more foreign under-21 players for SPL matches. The idea is to raise that limit to 14 or more, with discussions still ongoing.

Should the new rule come into force, Saudi clubs are likely to make more international signings. That could mark a new phase of departures from Europe to join the Saudi project, which aims to improve the competitive level of local football before the country hosts the World Cup in 2034.

In January 2023, Cristiano Ronaldo joined Al-Nassr after terminating his contract with Manchester United, which began a series of Saudi investments in football. In June of that year, the Public Investment Fund (PIF) took control of the four biggest domestic clubs: Al-Ahli, Al-Hilal, Al-Ittihad and Al-Nassr, the Portuguese star's team.

Then Ballon d'Or winner Karim Benzema was another high-profile name to leave Real Madrid for the Saudi Pro League, followed by stars such as N'Golo Kante and Roberto Firmino. Over the past three seasons, Neymar, Ollie Watkins, Gabriel Martinelli, Tijjani Reijnders, Darwin Nunez, Ivan Toney, Sadio Mane and Joao Felix have also been tempted by the Middle East.

As well as drawing global attention to its league, Saudi Arabia believes the move has helped the development of its homegrown talent. Competing for starting places with foreign stars encourages local players to improve.

On the other hand, critics of the proposal to raise the limit on non-Saudi players argue that the rule change could force local players to move abroad, or even leave bigger clubs for smaller ones, in order to get playing time.

It is worth remembering that the PIF has reduced its international sports investments, to the point of ending its backing of LIV Golf. In April, the fund announced a five-year programme with a greater focus on domestic investment. Privatisations of Saudi clubs have also been recurring, such as the sale of 70 per cent of Al-Hilal in August.

Because of the geopolitical context in the region, including Saudi Arabia's conflict with the Yemen-based Houthi rebels, there is some uncertainty over the league's ability to attract foreign players in the short term. In October, the airport in the capital, Riyadh, was hit by a missile attack that killed 13 people and injured more than 300.

The Asian Cup, which was due to be held in the country between January and February 2027, was postponed earlier this month. Three SPL matches were also postponed after the October Houthi attacks, although organisers did not attribute the decision to the conflict, saying it was motivated by 'logistical considerations'.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm

Instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

As for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

This was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

Arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

In fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh

All that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be said that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a big summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

“Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

Arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

In the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

For the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN

Chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

Ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

“It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

“After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

“It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0

"He's not the goalkeeper that won the World Cup" 🏆Jamie Carragher says Emi Martinez is not as quick or sharp as he once was 🧤 pic.twitter.com/SOp4XhoYIr

“I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it does not look like anyone can score against them.

“There is a massive gulf between both teams; their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today. We do not normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They are so strong defensively they do not need to get involved in those games.

“They still did not look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box.”

“It was a massive game with a tough opponent. It was really hard for us; we got there in the end. Our mentality is to keep fighting. Conceding early was not ideal but we reacted really well. We played well in the second half and got our reward. We showed our quality today. The result reflected that.”

“He is a really smart player and moves so well. He takes defenders attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind I am always free. It was a brilliant goal.”

“We knew Arsenal were the better team and they have proven that in this game. The question before today was, how close are Chelsea? And [Xabi] Alonso will be proud of what he has seen. There are obviously improvements to be made, but they gave it a right good go. A lot of very good things and they will be frustrated and disappointed, but they may potentially look back on this game as a good moment rather than as bad as it may feel right now.”
