#1561. Southampton vs Middlesbrough - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 25 Nov 2026 10:10

Southampton and Middlesbrough square off at St Mary's on Friday night in their first showdown since the conclusion of the Spygate saga.

While the visitors sit at the top of the Championship table, the Saints are just seven points adrift of opponents who are now viewed as one of their fierce rivals.

More than six months on from Tonda Eckert being found guilty of launching a spying mission on a Middlesbrough training session ahead of their playoff semi-final, Southampton have moved on from the controversy that rocked English football.

While Eckert will accept the attention that Friday's game attracts, he will remain focused on trying to secure promotion to the Premier League.

Despite being docked four points as part of their punishment from the Football Association, Southampton can move to within four points of Boro with victory on the South coast.

That said, the Saints have struggled for consistency of late, only collecting five points from four games and conceding a late equaliser to draw 1-1 at Sheffield United on Tuesday night.

Nevertheless, Southampton have been sensational at their home ground. Not only have 22 points being accumulated from a possible 24, they have scored 22 goals and conceded just five.

As for Middlesbrough, they make the long trip south having collected 12 points from eight fixtures, albeit only prevailing on three occasions.

Eight goals had been scored in back-to-back away successes at Stoke City and Bolton Wanderers, yet Kim Hellberg's side have failed to score in the last two such contests versus Wrexham and Watford.

However, 2-0 and 2-1 successes over Bristol City and Swansea City at the Riverside Stadium have ensured that Boro enter this game in top spot with 34 goals from their 17 matches.

Will Lankshear's return from a minor injury may also prove key. Despite being limited to a 62-minute outing versus Swansea, he netted his 14th Championship goal of the season.

Eckert will recall a number of his Southampton regulars for this contest, with Jack Stephens, Ryan Manning and Finn Azaz among those who will start.

James Bree may also feature on the back of his 30-minute outing versus Sheffield United after a minor injury, but Leo Scienza is likely to be named on the substitutes' bench at best after missing the last two matches.

Centre-back Keven Schlotterbeck will be sidelined until December through injury.

As for Boro, Sebastian Berhalter is expected to return in central midfield, with Myles Peart-Harris potentially being used further forward.

Providing that Lankshear shows no ill-effects from Tuesday's game, he should start, with David Strelec likely dropping down to the bench to accommodate an extra midfielder.

Despite concerns over an ankle injury, Neto Borges came through 90 minutes versus Swansea and seems in line to be selected at left-back.

Peretz; Roerslav, Abbott, Stephens, Manning; Downes, Ward-Prowse; Matsuki, Azaz, Dobbin; Larin

Vitek; Brittain, Phillips, Malanda, Borges; Morris, Berhalter; Cozier-Duberry, Peart-Harris, McGree; Lankshear

Although Boro have returned from the November international break with back-to-back wins, we cannot ignore the intensity that these two teams will play at during this contest. That, and home advantage, may favour Southampton, leading us to predict a narrow victory for Eckert's side in a game that will include plenty of cautions.

#1560. KILMARNOCK 2 ABERDEEN 4: Dazzling Dons get a Frick pick-up but it's more misery for McCann's men

Published: 15:33 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026

Having been bored senseless by the football offered up under Stephen Robinson, Aberdeen supporters were – at the very least – crying out for the next appointment to provide some sort of entertainment to get excited about over the dark winter months.

In Mario Frick, they may have got their man. Whether or not the former Luzern boss will be a success at Pittodrie is anyone’s guess. But on this evidence, it’s going to be a lot of fun watching him have a go.

At times, they were scintillating here on their way to a thrilling win which moved them five clear of their hosts and provided some much-needed breathing room ahead of a tricky upcoming schedule which involves trips to Ibrox and Tynecastle, as well as two home clashes against the Dundee clubs.

Yes, it wasn’t perfect. Far from it, in fact. Defensively, they were far too open. Kilmarnock just weren’t good enough to take full advantage.

But you suspect that will be forgiven to an extent as long as they can play with this level of panache and aggression going forward.

Findlay Marshall celebrates after scoring the Dons' fourth goal at Rugby Park

Frick has arrived with the promise of bringing ‘heavy metal’ football to Pittodrie. It’s taken a little over 90 minutes to understand what he's talking about.

‘It was very chaotic,’ he admitted. ‘It's quite different to Switzerland, because there is technicality, but it’s not as physical as it was today.

‘It was difficult. We were lucky as well because Killie, especially in the second half, played very well, but I think at the end it's a deserved victory.

‘When the players were young, they didn’t think about mistakes, didn’t think about any negatives.

‘They played only to win for fun, and I told them to play as if they were young players and I think, especially first half, it was very good.

‘You don't know what's going on or what can happen in this first game, so I'm very happy we won.’

Frick shows his delight after tasting victory in his first match in charge of Aberdeen

Kilmarnock spurned a golden opportunity to take a sixth-minute lead at the end of a rapid counter-attack, with Joe Hugill finding himself all alone in the Dons box.

The striker took a heavy first touch, allowing Marius Muller to quickly narrow the angle and block the effort. It’s easy to see why Hugill has found the back of the net just twice this year.

And the hosts were made to pay for that miss within 90 seconds as Aberdeen went in front.

For the umpteenth time this season, Killie failed to clear their lines under little pressure, with Stuart Armstrong teeing up Kevin Nisbet to sweep home a lovely finish from the edge of the area. The unsighted Nico Mantl in the Killie goal didn’t even move.

Mind you, he should have done significantly better four minutes later as Nisbet notched his second of the afternoon.

The keeper’s positioning as the Dons striker stepped up to send a low free-kick in off the post was as poor as it gets.

You got the feeling that the walls would have caved in had Aberdeen grabbed a third, but a brief drop-off in intensity from Frick’s side enabled Killie to drag themselves back into the contest.

A bit of pinball outside the Dons box saw the ball fall favourably for skipper Greg Kiltie 12 yards out, who adjusted his body brilliantly to drill beyond Muller on the half-volley.

Yet with a defence as dodgy as this, manager Neil McCann can never feel overly confident.

Ante Palaversa – terrific on his first appearance of the season – was given far too much time in the centre circle to get his head up and pick out Nesta Guinness-Walker on the left.

He glided past MJ Kamson-Kamara as if he wasn’t there before dinking a ball right on to the head of Brad Lyons, who rose completely unopposed to power home against his former employers.

If Killie continue to defend like this, relegation is a certainty. Will the manager even get the chance to turn it around? Going off the abuse being hurled in his direction from the home punters, his jacket is evidently on a shoogly peg. Many fans have already made up their mind.

Nisbet's free-kick finds the net for his second as the Dons take control of the game

Michael Schjonning-Larsen’s deflected effort from 20 yards shortly after the restart looked destined for the goal before Muller instinctively leapt to his right to claw it away on the line. It was a superb stop.

Goodness knows what the keeper was thinking as he tried to pass out from the six-yard line, playing it straight to the feet of Tyreece John-Jules – only just on the park – who steadied himself before finishing.

You would have stuck your house on Nisbet putting this one to bed with five minutes remaining, however with just Mantl to beat, he pulled his left-footed effort wide.

Findlay Marshall showed him how it’s done with stoppage-time looming, running half the length of the field before drilling low into the corner to consign Killie to another sobering defeat.

McCann said: ‘I probably sound like a broken record, but we create really big, big chances, and we don't take them.

‘We're letting games pass us by. We're giving teams the opportunity to start ahead of us because of the goals we're conceding and then it's difficult to work back.’

#1558. African Player of the Year 2026: Final shortlist revealed without Ismaila Sarr

By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 11:02

On Tuesday night, in Dakar, it was possible to seriously imagine Ismaila Sarr lifting the African Ballon d'Or. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) had just confirmed Senegal's triumph at the Africa Cup of Nations, and the Crystal Palace winger saw his candidacy significantly strengthened.

Yet the next day, his name had disappeared from the list. The Confederation of African Football (CAF) selected Sadio Mane and Pape Gueye on the Senegalese side, along with Achraf Hakimi, Brahim Diaz and Ismael Saibari for Morocco.

?????? ?? ??? ???? (???) - ????????? #CAFAwards2026 https://t.co/RcZAogxLza

A winner of the Conference League with Crystal Palace, Sarr also finished as the competition's top scorer with nine goals and was named the best player of the tournament.

At the World Cup, he scored four times, including a goal against Belgium in the round of 32. He has a total of 24 goals and five assists in 53 games in 2026, for club and country. That annual record goes beyond the period assessed by CAF, which ended on 15 September. His European title and his World Cup, however, fell within that window, as did the Africa Cup of Nations triumph, even though its validation only came after the fact.

Pape Gueye scored the goal that won the Africa Cup of Nations for Senegal and features in the team of the tournament. Sadio Mane, the winner in 2019 and 2022, was named the best player of this Africa Cup of Nations. Their places are defensible.

But if the three Senegalese had to be separated over the whole period, Sarr's case, decisive at club level and at the World Cup, appears more complete. He had what it took to aim for first place. Seeing him miss out on the top five is hard to understand.

The CAS ruling revived that hope in Senegal when voting had already closed. CAF had set the end of voting for 20 November, four days before the verdict.

Achraf Hakimi remains the favourite among the five selected. The 2025 winner, the full-back won a second consecutive Champions League with Paris Saint-Germain and reached the World Cup quarter-finals with Morocco.

Brahim Diaz finished as the top scorer at the Africa Cup of Nations with five goals. His missed Panenka in the final remains the most striking image of his tournament, after he had found the net in five games in a row.

Ismael Saibari, meanwhile, scored against Brazil, Scotland and Haiti. He became the first African to score in each of his country's three group games at a single World Cup. Currently injured, the Bayern player can therefore also hope for a crowning at the ceremony on 2 December in Lagos.

#1557. Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s new era lift-off

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

Suzuki, the £30m replacement for Emiliano Martínez, has clear presence in goal and he is Villa’s version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson with his wide array of passing.

Gomes was also industrious in midfield to recover from what was a nightmarish debut at Brighton, where he was sent off after 40 minutes.

Despite all the changes to this team, talismanic captain John McGinn remains essential to Villa. He became their all-time leading goalscorer in major European competitions with his 12th goal and led by example again, as he has done so many times.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

There were also hints of a strong defensive partnership developing between Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof, following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

“Fantastic, fantastic,” purred Emery at one point in the second half from the technical area, and Villa’s season now appears up and running.

Emery said: “This was another step forward and I am so happy and thankful for this. The old players need to keep our standards high and show everyone this is the only way we can achieve the process and reach our targets.

“It’s very important to start the Champions League with three points and hopefully this will give us confidence for the league. We are improving and we must work hard – it is the only way.”

Although Emery has established a reputation as the Europa League king, winning that trophy five times, this competition has proved more difficult to master.

His best run was reaching the semi-finals in the 2021-22 season, when his Villarreal side lost to Liverpool.

It remains a tournament in which he is desperate to make an impression, with Villa returning to Champions League duty here for the first time since their thrilling encounter with Paris St-Germain in April 2025.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

They had only managed one shot on target so far this season before arriving in this historic city, but scored three goals before half-time.

Their opener came against the run of play in the 11th minute, with McGinn casually finding the corner after a lung-bursting run from Torres. McGinn has overtaken former Villa striker Ollie Watkins at the top of the club’s continental goalscoring charts.

Brugge briefly wobbled but were level eight minutes later when Hugo Vetlesen swept home from 10 yards, capitalising on space in the penalty box.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

Villa were back in front less than 160 seconds later, with Gomes teeing up Emiliano Buendía for an easy finish. Gomes was released in the box by a clever backheel from Jackson.

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Two minutes before half-time Yann Sommer, Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper, then had a severe rush of blood to the head by racing from his goal to almost the halfway line in an attempt to intercept Torres’s long pass.

Jackson edged the ball past him and held off a defender to calmly slot into the empty net. He underlined in many moments why Emery has pursued him for so long, after the pair established a strong rapport at Villarreal.

Villa appeared relatively comfortable in the second half until Aaron Wan-Bissaka was judged to have handled a cross from Joaquin Seys, after referee Sandro Schärer was advised by VAR to review the incident on his TV monitor.

It was a simple decision and Nicolò Tresoldi put away the penalty to stir life back into the home supporters.

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Villa defended resolutely as time began to tick away with Suzuki providing authority in goal. The first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Champions League also produced a number of routine saves in a nervy finish.

This was a promising night for a new Villa era.

Full-time scenes in Bruges as Aston Villa get their Champions League campaign off to a winning start! 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nYwtiQ6Xs7

Villa are defending with six at the back as midfield and defence merge into one. There are seconds remaining as Suzuki punts the ball up field and there is the final whistle! Villa make a winning start to the 2026-27 Champions League.

Another cross from the right is met, this time, by Tresoldi, but his header has no bite and Suzuki gathers.

Torres heads another Siquet cross behind for a corner. Brugge load the box but none of their players are able to get a meaningful touch on the ball before Diakhon slips just as he looks to get a shot away from the left of the box.

Slightly less mature play from Gomes, though. He bundles Vermant over and earns a needless yellow card.

Really mature play by Hemmings. Looking to break away, he simply puts his body between man and ball, inviting the challenge and winning a foul.

Villa are working hard in their compact mid-block and Brugge are struggling to find a way through.

Leko sends on Vermant and Diakhon for Potts and Virgili.

Barkley is one lucky boy. Attempting to play out under pressure, the midfielder gives the ball straight to Virgili, who cannot sort out his feet before offloading to Tresoldi far too late. A big let-off for Villa.

Gomes goes close after driving through Brugge’s midfield. He really should, though, have played in a free McGinn at the back post. Moments later Bogarde fires another shot goalwards but Sommer gets to it.

Villa have wrestled control away from their opponents. McGinn’s teasing cross evades everyone and Alysson’s cross takes a deflection which goes behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Lee hauls down Hemmings which gives Villa the opportunity to slow the game down. McGinn flights a delivery in from the left but Brugge clear their lines.

The ball comes out to Alysson who jinks in from the right, tiptoeing through a crowd, desperate to get a shot away on his left foot, but Seys does well to track his man and smother the effort.

Vanakan and Velesen and replaced by Tsawa and Lemarechal.

Yet another dangerous Siquet cross rains in from the right and here it is taken off Tresoldi’s toes by the tip of Lindelof’s boot. The defender did brilliantly to clear his lines at full stretch.

Hemmings burst towards the by-line and his cross trickles across the face of goal. Alysson is waiting at the far post but Seys does well to shield the ball and win a free-kick.

Villa’s best chance at putting this game to bed will come on the counter. And here McGinn plays in Jackson whose one-vs-one effort is stopped by Sommer.

Virgili from the left, Siquet from the right. Threats are coming from both wings and Villa need to get their foot on the ball if they are to take the sting out of Brugge’s attack.

Instead they allow Vetlesen a yard of space and his long-range sighter stings the hands of Suzuki who turns behind for a corner.

Emery switches out Buendia, Kamara and Wan-Bissaka for Alysson, Barkley and Bogarde before the corner is taken, and Suzuki stops the eventual delivery on the line after the ball spun off the post!

Another Virgili cross threatens to carve Villa open but they just about clear their lines. Then it is Siquet who delivers, this time from the right, but his cross just evades Tresoldi and Mechele at the far post. The home fans are invested in this, they believe their side can grab an equaliser...

Villa have got their tails between their legs here. From a position of strength, they have allowed the momentum to swing in the hosts’ favour and it has been largely self-inflicted.

Maatsen has a chance to break free but cannot build a head of steam before he is stymied.

Club Brugge 2 Aston Villa 3 (Tresoldi pen) Suzuki dives to his right early and Tresoldi slides the ball into the opposite side of the net. Just the one goal in it now!

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Brugge have averted their attention to their right hand side, Siquet and Forbs attacking in tandem. A dangerous cross from Forbs is met by Tresoldi but he cannot get the requisite contact on it. Seys collects the ball on the far side and fires a delivery into Wan-Bissaka and out for a corner. Replays show that it comes off the defenders hand ...and referee Scharer is sent to the screen. He wastes no time at the monitor and awards a spot kick!

Villa do appear pretty comfortable here, despite some frequent pressure from Club Brugge.

Pau Torres has been outstanding so far at the back for Unai Emery’s team.

This is also a night where Emery’s ‘new’ Villa are coming of age, with Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and Joao Gomes also impressive.

Virgili then darts in field from his starting perch on the left. Tresoldi backheels the ball back into his path but Virgili’s effort is snuffed out.

McGinn, sensing Virgili’s growing influence on the half, takes matters into his own hands and leaves one on the Spanish winger, Siquet’s free-kick from deep is aimed at Tresoldi but Suzuki is wise to it and sweeps up.

Brugge are just reminding Villa that they are still there. Virgili is at the heart of things again, combining with Vetlesen who works the ball out to Forbs whose cross is well held by Suzuki.

Villa then spring forward, Hemmings breaching the Brugge box, but Buendia’s eventual effort does not make it through a thicket of legs.

Brugge are building with a three-man backline, sending Siquet forward high and wide. They’ve had much of the ball in the opening stages of this half, which is probably part of Villa’s plan. Emery’s side have settled into an out-of-possession 4-4-2.

Vanakan is booked for simulation after going hitting the deck off a challenge from Gomes. There is a knowing smile on the Belgian midfielder’s face which suggests the referee’s convictions were correct.

We are back under way... Siquet replaces Sabbe at the interval.

Nicolas Jackson is off the mark for Aston Villa. He beat Yann Sommer to the ball, held off a defender and was left with the simplest of finishes to round off a fine first half for Villa. pic.twitter.com/gWx6kUTlOX

Unai Emery has the new kids on the block but this Aston Villa team are hangin’ tough.

This has been a pretty chaotic first-half on the return of the Champions League but Emery will be satisfied with what he has seen so far. It’s very much a case of step by step for his reshaped team, but they should see this game out now.

It’s been a shocking night for Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper Yann Sommer. He’s just had a serious rush of blood to the head and was punished by Nicolas Jackson, who had an easy task to score Villa’s third goal. Sommer has probably ended his team’s hopes of a result here.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 3 (Jackson) A shocker from Brugge, but in particular Sommer. Jackson races on to a nothing punt over the top by Torres, and the situation appears under control with two defenders in the striker’s orbit, but Sommer comes steaming out and Jackson nudges the ball past him before sliding it home into a vacant net.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

A sloppy Torres pass out from the back goes straight to Vetlesen who picks out Forbs first time. The winger unleashes an effort from range but Suzuki makes a smart stop.

There is a shout for a Villa handball as Virgili prods a cross on to Kamara’s body, but his arms are clearly by his side.

Villa are presented with a great opportunity to break but the pass in behind for Jackson to gallop on to does not have enough juice and the move breaks down. Jackson does have a sight at goal moments later, but he’s only able to poke the ball wide off a free-kick from the right.

A really sloppy piece bit of play from Vanakan who cedes possession to Jackson and he’s straight into Brugge’s backline. He releases the ball to McGinn but the midfielder’s looping cross is cleared. Brugge need to take better care with the detail on their passes.

Jackson escapes the clutches of his marker on the half-way line with a deft spin and he feeds McGinn whose shot is blocked. The ball is worked to Hemmings after Torres is afforded space once more and a block takes it behind for a corner. Villa go short but the routine comes to nothing.

Maatsen flashes a dangerous delivery across the face of goal but the ball bisects Jackson and Buendia precisely and Brugge are able to clear their lines.

Brugge have certainly not given up the ghost, still looking to work the ball out to Forbs and Virgili on the flanks. Sabbe overlaps down the right but his ball to Vetlesen is cut out and Villa attempt to spring a counter which is snuffed out by Mechele.

Villa midfielder Joao Gomes is having a productive evening as he aims to recover from that nightmare debut.

He was sent off after 40 minutes of his first Villa appearance in the excruciating 4-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion.

Unai Emery is expecting big things from the Brazilian midfielder, who departed relegated Wolves for £38m in July.

Wan-Bissaka drives down the right as Villa look for a third, but his cross is overhit and goes off on the far side. The right intent, though.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 2 (Buendia) Jackson holds up the ball expertly before slipping in Gomes. The midfielder bursts into the box, outwitting Vetlesen before cutting the ball back to an onrushing Buendia who clips the ball past Sommer with aplomb. A crazy couple of minutes!

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 1 (Vetlesen) Brugge are getting a lot of joy down the flanks. This time it is Vetlesen who finds space down the right and he spears a cross into the box. The ball is worked out to the left where the dangerous Virgili sends the ball back into the area and there Vetlesen is to sweep home. The stadium erupts as the Belgian champions restore parity.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

The Jan Breydelstadion had been very noisy but that goal has completely changed the atmosphere.

It is now nervy in the stadium and the Brugge fans are already starting to boo some of their players.

Villa’s first goal of the season and no surprise it comes from their talisman John McGinn.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

Close! Hemmings races on to a cutback but his effort trickles just wide of the post.

Goalkeeper Sommer is penalised for handling the ball outside of his box. He had gathered a corner and had stormed forward to set off an attack. He changes his mind mid-throw and attempts to re-catch the ball but ends up wandering outside of his allotted space. The resulting free-kick crashes straight into the wall.

Sommer with an accidental handball outside his area! 😳📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fBbqPEYyUJ

Club Brugge 0 Aston Villa 1 (McGinn) Brugge will be really disappointed with that. Torres is afforded the freedom of Flanders as he strides up from his own half to the edge of the hosts’ box. He offloads the ball to McGinn on the right of the area and the Scotsman steadies himself before curling the ball into the far post, beyond Sommer.

It is that duo again, Virgili and Seys. They have responded to Wan-Bissaka’s advanced position and are trying to pin him back. Virgili cuts in on to his right foot and forces a save from Suzuki to get the home fans going.

Aston Villa are still establishing their identity with a new team but it has already become clear how much they will rely on goalkeeper Zion Suzuki,

The £30m signing from Parma possesses a wide passing range and much of Villa’s build-up play starts with the Japan international.

He is Villa’s very own version of Manchester City’s former pass master Ederson.

Much has been made of Suzuki’s distribution and he has already teased a couple of lovely flighted balls up-field. Villa’s defenders are more than happy to lure Brugge’s first line of pressure forward but have not yet been able to find an incisive line-breaking pass.

Seyes and Virgili combine down the left in Brugge’s best attack so far, but Torres is able to head behind for a corner, which is not up to much.

Wan-Bissaka has taken up a very aggressive position down Villa’s right and he earns a free-kick in a promising position. McGinn spins in a delivery which is only partially cleared but Maatsen’s effort from the edge of the box is smothered.

Villa get their foot on the ball from the get-go, circulating the ball around the back, before Suzuki launches a long ball up to Wan-Bissaka. The ball is worked to McGinn who feeds Buendia on the edge of the box but his effort flies just wide.

There is a minute’s silence for those affected by the floods in Nepal which is impeccably observed.

The players then retreat to their halves and Jackson gets us going!

Brugge and Villa emerge from the tunnel to the Champions League anthem... Here is this season’s introductory VT to whet the appetite.

The Champions League is back. #UCL pic.twitter.com/bsFGV69KMP

"This is a good test and challenge for us today." 💪Aston Villa boss Unai Emery looks ahead to their Champions League clash with Club Brugge.🎙️ @LiamMacdevitt | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h4NF1jmiW6

As the rain lashes down in Bruges, you get the sense that Villa will have to dig deep to get a result and breathe life into their season. Both teams thrive on attacking transitions and the surface-level moisture will encourage breakaway moves.

Quite the evening, last time out at the Jan Breydel Stadium 💫 pic.twitter.com/NogGLLSMFU

Opta’s supercomputer has worked its magic again this season and placed Villa as the 10th favourites to lift the Champions League trophy. Back-to-back winners Paris St-Germain are only fifth. Here are the leading contenders before a ball has been kicked.

Agree? Leave your thoughts in the comments section beneath this live blog...

Aston Villa 2.0 is clearly a work in progress after so many high-profile exits and 10 new signings.

Unai Emery has warned that it will take time for his new team to click, but this is an opportunity to spark the season into life.

Behind the scenes, Villa are feeling very comfortable about so much upheaval and it is the presence of Emery in the technical area which provides them with so much optimism.

For a deeper dive into why patience will be needed, read more here.

Brugge have conceded just two goals in five league games this season, but their Pro League opponents have threatened against the Belgian champions’ right side, especially in attacking transitions. Kyriani Sabbe is the more adventurous of Brugge’s two full-backs and the space he vacates will be inviting to George Hemmings and Ian Maatsen.

Here are a couple of examples of Brugge’s vulnerability down their right:

Don-Angelo Konadu, Lommel’s centre-forward, drifts out to the left and takes on Lee Han-beom whose centre-back partner Brandon Mechele has committed too far forward. As such, the space between Lee and covering left-back Joaquin Seys is too big and Freddie Potts attempts to recover from midfield. Konadu earns himself a yard with a feint inside and his shot is well-saved by Yann Sommer.

In Brugge’s 2-1 defeat by Gent a week earlier, Leonardo Lopes punches in a pass into the left half-space for Monodu Sonko to latch on to and from there the inside forward draws a save from Sommer. Josué Vergara’s follow-up strikes the crossbar.

The Spaniard added a fifth Europa League title to his CV last season while also guiding Villa to a strong fourth-place finish in the Premier League. Emery was today announced as one of five nominees for France Football’s Men’s Coach of the Year award – one of the Ballon d’Or accolades.

Christos Tzolis enjoyed an outstanding season with Brugge in 2025-26, contributing 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. His haul earned him a £34m move to Arsenal, where he has continued in much the same vein, laying on three assists in four matches.

While Tzolis wears the No 17 at Arsenal, his former No 8 shirt at Brugge has been inherited by Englishman Freddie Potts, who made the move from West Ham to Belgium last month. Potts has made a strong start to the season, serving as Brugge’s midfield sentry and starting all five of the club’s matches thus far.

One player to keep an eye on for Club Brugge is midfielder Freddie Potts.

He was signed from West Ham last month for a significant fee and lifted the Europa Conference League trophy when David Moyes was in charge.

Also in the Brugge team is Carlos Forbs, the former Manchester City trainee who had a poor loan spell at Wolves a couple of seasons back.

Club Brugge Sommer; Sabbe, Lee, Mechele, Seys; Potts, Vanaken; Forbs, Vetlesen, Virgili; Tresoldi

Substitutes Audoor, Coulibaly, Diakhon, Jackers, Lemarechal, Mike, Siquet, Spileers, Tsawa, Vanden Driessche, Vasovic, Vermant

Aston Villa Suzuki; Wan-Bissaka, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; McGinn, Buendia, Hemmings; Jackson

One player who will have many memories of this stadium is Villa centre-back Tyrone Mings.

Who can forget that bewildering moment in November 2024 when Mings picked up the ball inside the penalty area?

Club Brugge are awarded a penalty after Tyrone Mings picks the ball up inside his own area 😳📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/wpAqjMW8pn

Everybody loves a redemption story and on his return a few months later he produced a brilliant individual performance which included an incredible goal-line clearance to save his team.

Mings is on the bench today. Matty Cash is out with a muscle issue so there is a first start for summer signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Addressing the media in Monday’s pre-match press conference, Unai Emery was asked about the challenges of taking Aston Villa into another season in Europe with a significantly changed squad. He said: “To continue in this level, changing some players, key players, but those key players we changed this year as well before the last year we were changing – not like this year, because this year was more players than normal, but we are replacing them.

“We have the players with experience like here with Emiliano [Buendía] and they deserve to continue here trying take now more responsibility and try to give the players we have … Of course we have now new players with a lot of experience like Goretska for example, and we have some young players, they are coming from [big] clubs like Garnacho, Mbaye or Jackson. We must try to adapt them in our structure tactically and arrive [at that point] as fast as possible … We need time, I don’t know if we need time or not, it’s not for me something I’m thinking about, I am thinking about competing. To compete [in] each match.

“We started the Premier League, the first competition, as our objective at the end of the season, because through it we can achieve our objectives this year, and we’re progressing. Still not enough, because we are not getting good results. But [the match against Brugge] is a new test.”

The experienced Yann Sommer starts between the sticks, with in-form striker Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line. English midfielder Freddie Potts is one of Ivan Leko’s two pivots.

Our ground crew for tonight. 👥📃 pic.twitter.com/UB7FUi9ZDH

Emery makes three changes from the XI that started against Hull City. Wan-Bissaka comes in for Matty Cash who does not make the match-day squad. Joao Gomes is eligible to play despite being suspended in domestic competition while Pau Torres replaces Tyrone Mings.

How we start this evening to take on Club Brugge in the #UCL 👊 pic.twitter.com/d7ftzgnoIi

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a new-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of big-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s new-look crew.

Morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his new recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

It seems AC Milan have made an offer for Endrick in recent days, with a Spanish journalist shocked at the situation.

Talk of Endrick arriving at San Siro is dominating the news, and it’s clear that Milan are not messing around here. Indeed, they are looking to beat off interest from other European clubs and they may well be close to doing so.

Jose Mourinho is still opposing a deal, but the Brazilian’s entourage was in Italy last week and it seems that a move to San Siro is becoming less of a hypothetical and more of a tangible possibility.

Speaking to SER Radio, Anton Meana looked at the reporting from Italy about the Rossoneri’s interest in Endrick and how the situation was actually unfolding.

“AC Milan’s offer is formal and they want to sign him in January. The Rossoneri have already informed the player, and if he can’t leave in January, they’ll see about negotiations in the summer. But AC Milan’s firm offer is now on the table.

“The owner of AC Milan wants to offer close to 70 million euros to sign Endrick now. The problem is that Mourinho prefers to keep him because he knows there wouldn’t be a signing that could match or surpass the Brazilian.

“It’s good for him to have Endrick because he’s good, because he provides competition for Mbappé, and because he trains hard for every match. I want to see how the next few weeks unfold. I’d say Endrick isn’t going to leave, but the player’s entourage, his agents, will be in Madrid this week or early next week seeking talks and exploring the striker’s immediate future.

“I thought it was just the typical bluff from the Italian transfer press, who constantly promote players and see them as being in Serie A all the time, but this offer from Milan, I honestly didn’t expect it. The interest, as Cerruti told you, is very serious, and if they can, they want to sign Endrick this winter transfer window.”

It’s safe to say that the Diavolo’s interest is more than speculative and with an official offer on the table, things may begin to move between Milan and Madrid.

#1555. Manchester City favourites to sign Borussia Dortmund star after formal approach

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Manchester City are continuing to invest in young talent as they look to strengthen their squad for the future, with another exciting prospect emerging on their transfer radar.

Pep Guardiola’s side have reportedly moved into pole position for one of Borussia Dortmund’s most highly rated youngsters.

United States international Mathis Albert has attracted interest from several European clubs, but City are currently considered the favourites to secure his signature.

With the teenager’s first-team opportunities limited in Germany, the Premier League champions could look to take advantage of the situation.

According to TEAMtalk, Manchester City are the frontrunners to sign Albert after making a formal approach during the summer transfer window.

The report claims City are prepared to offer the 17-year-old lucrative personal terms as they step up their pursuit. Their interest is serious, with the club previously prepared to meet a valuation in the region of €20 million (£16.7m).

Chelsea are also long-term admirers of the youngster and were reportedly willing to spend a similar amount last winter. Paris Saint-Germain previously made contact with Dortmund in 2025, while Arsenal and Liverpool have more recently been monitoring his situation.

However, City are currently viewed as being in the strongest position should Dortmund soften their stance.

Albert joined Borussia Dortmund from the LA Galaxy academy in 2024 and has quickly established himself as one of the most exciting young American talents in European football. He has already made Bundesliga appearances and earned senior international recognition with the United States.

Despite his potential, opportunities under Niko Kovac have been limited this season. That lack of regular first-team football has encouraged several clubs to monitor his development, although Dortmund remain determined to keep hold of their young attacker.

The Bundesliga side have reportedly rejected approaches, including loan enquiries, and continue to view Albert as an important part of their long-term plans. They are also preparing a contract extension offer, with his current agreement running until June 2027.

There is another important factor for City. Premier League regulations prevent English clubs from signing Albert permanently until he turns 18 in May, meaning any potential transfer would be geared towards next summer rather than an immediate move.

Tottenham could face growing interest in one of their key players ahead of the January transfer window, with Barcelona president Joan Laporta reportedly keen on bringing Pedro Porro to the Nou Camp.

The Spanish right-back has attracted attention following his performances for Spain at the World Cup, but Spurs have several reasons to feel confident about keeping hold of the defender.

According to Catalan broadcaster 3Cat, Porro is one of Laporta’s preferred defensive targets as Barcelona consider whether to strengthen their backline in January.

The Catalan club have been dealing with a series of defensive injuries involving Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde, Andreas Christensen and Xavi Espart. However, Barcelona have not made a final decision on whether to bring in another defender, with the club waiting to assess the injured players’ recoveries.

Laporta’s admiration for Porro reportedly grew during Spain’s World Cup campaign. The Tottenham defender became an important part of the national team, developing a strong understanding with Lamine Yamal on the right flank and scoring twice during the tournament, including in the semi-final against France.

Laporta watched that semi-final in Dallas and was reportedly impressed by Porro’s performance. Barcelona had also gathered information about the defender towards the end of the previous summer transfer window, but their enquiry did not progress into a formal proposal to either the player or Tottenham.

Porro’s contractual situation gives Spurs a strong negotiating position. The 27-year-old renewed his contract shortly before the World Cup, committing his future to the north London club until 2031.

Reports have also indicated that Tottenham would demand a significant fee to consider allowing the defender to leave. Real Madrid have also been linked with an interest in the Spain international, potentially creating further competition for his signature.

#1553. Leeds transfer news: Will Lankshear January hopes shot down by 44-goal striker

By Ben Knapton | 25 Nov 2026 11:33

Former Leeds United striker Brian Deane, speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, has played down the Whites' chances of signing Will Lankshear in the January transfer window.

The former Tottenham Hotspur youngster has taken the Championship by storm since moving to the Riverside Stadium in the summer, scoring 14 goals in 15 second-tier appearances.

Lankshear netted the winner as Middlesbrough beat Swansea City 2-1 on Tuesday night, a result that saw Kim Hellberg's men move one point clear of Wolverhampton Wanderers at the top of the Championship table.

The 21-year-old unsurprisingly sits top of the Championship top scorers charts, three clear of closest challenger Andri Gudjohnsen of Blackburn Rovers in the race for the Golden Boot.

Lankshear's form has inevitably led to speculation surrounding a swift return to the Premier League, with multiple clubs believed to be interested in securing his services, including Leeds.

Former club Tottenham, Arsenal, Brighton & Hove Albion and Newcastle United have also been credited with an interest, although Middlesbrough's £70m asking price could deter suitors.

Now, former Leeds forward Deane - who scored 44 goals in 199 matches for the Whites - has expressed his view that Lankshear should remain at the Riverside Stadium over the winter.

“This is his breakout season, and he is at a good club," Deane told Sports Mole. "Middlesbrough look on course to challenge for promotion, so hopefully he gets there with them.

“He will be ambitious and attract attention from clubs such as Leeds, Brighton and Newcastle. He would be a good addition to a squad. But for his own development, I think he is in a good place at Middlesbrough.”

Lankshear made just six senior appearances for Tottenham before being sold in a £9.8m deal over the summer, and the striker's contract with Middlesbrough does not expire until 2031.

A young striker scoring for fun in the Championship will always attract glances from top-tier clubs, but Lankshear may struggle to force his way into Daniel Farke's first XI right now.

First-choice pairing Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Noah Okafor boast a respectable nine Premier League goals between them in 2026-27, and as long as both are fit, they will spearhead Farke's 3-5-2 system.

Calvert-Lewin is now in the final 24 months of his contract at Elland Road, but the England international is understood to be close to signing a new Leeds deal.

Lukas Nmecha also provides a steady backup option, although he is due to become a free agent in 2027 and may seek a move away in January if his game-time situation does not improve.

However, Nmecha's proposed exit would then open the door for summer signing Jean-Matteo Bahoya to earn more opportunities, so a winter move for Lankshear would make little sense for all involved.

Brian Deane was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of BetWright.

#1551. New system, same problems: Thomas Frank's first game in charge of Crystal Palace ends in defeat despite tactical switch... but Coventry are up to 13th

Published: 12:02 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:52 EST, 21 November 2026

Thomas Frank might have changed formation in his first game in charge of Crystal Palace, but there was no change in fortune for the Premier League’s bottom club.

There were, however, some noticeable improvements. Palace were more structured in attack, with cleverly orchestrated moves and a clear, coherent plan for creating chances.

But the same problem that plagued his predecessor Pierre Sage persisted: Palace cannot defend. That diagnosis is simple to make. However, addressing it is complicated by inadequate personnel.

Palace replaced Marc Guehi and Maxence Lacroix with teenage defender Honest Ahanor and Chelsea castoff Axel Disasi in the summer.

Until they can address the oversight in their squad planning - thinking that would be enough to replace two international centre-backs - they will continue to ship sloppy goals.

Frank will be able to address the structural problems, ensure players understand the positions they should occupy in specific situations and get Palace defending as a cohesive unit.

These are all things within his control and he began fixing them to some extent on Saturday.

Despite having a new manager in the dugout, the same old problems remained for Crystal Palace

His in-game management worked to a degree as Palace conceded two goals and defended frantically in the first half before looking much more solid and organised in the second period before finally conceding the decisive goal in the 85th minute.

What he won’t be able to eradicate, though, are the individual errors that have consistently cost Palace this season.

Ultimately, those mistakes come down to the quality of the defenders at his disposal.

Palace will look to address their personnel issues in January but they currently sit rock bottom of the league, with a massive game against Hull next Sunday.

Unless they can cut out the errors that have contributed to their 27 league goals conceded this season, they risk being cut adrift before they can bring in reinforcements.

New boss Frank was more glass-half-full, though. ‘There is more positive than negative from the game,’ Frank said. ‘We looked like a threat. We scored two very good goals and we created quite a few more chances to score at least one more goal.

‘That was the big positive. I was extremely happy with the effort and the mentality of the players.’

Defensively, this was a horror show. Three players were dragged out wide — including Disasi, who was miles out of position — allowing Jack Rudoni to find Taiwo Awoniyi in the penalty area to poke past Dean Henderson four minutes into Frank’s first assignment.

Coventry should have had a second, too, after Palace overcommitted in attack and Awoniyi was played in behind. One-on-one with Dean Henderson, he took the ball around the goalkeeper, only for Axel Disasi to somehow get back and clear it off the line.

Palace had been on the front foot but were caught out by how quickly they had to transition from attack to defence, unable to get enough bodies back in time. They are struggling to find a balance between defence and attack.

Dwight McNeil's own goal cost Palace late on as they slumped to a 3-2 defeat

Anan Khalaili failed to win his tackle for Coventry’s second, giving Rudoni space to run down the right. Nobody shut Rudoni down and he found Tatsuhiro Sakamoto, who rocketed a thunderous half-volley into the top corner from outside the area.

Coventry’s 85th-minute winner came from a long throw, which Palace failed to deal with.

Frank abandoned the back three, which had served Palace well for the last two years and nine months, and pivoted to a 4-2-3-1.

Offensively, Palace improved. The formation suited Yeremy Pino and Jorgen Strand Larsen particularly well, with the pair combining for both of Palace’s goals.

It should also bring the best out of Quinten Timber, Daichi Kamada and Adam Wharton, as individuals are rarely isolated in midfield, unlike under Pierre Sage.

On the other hand, Tyrick Mitchell and Khalaili still tried to function as wing-backs rather than full-backs.

That is ingrained in their habits, and it will take time to coach it out of them. However, it remains a significant issue.

Both players committed themselves forward when attacking, leaving an already fragile centre-back pairing exposed and allowing Coventry to transition quickly and exploit Palace's vulnerability.

That cannot happen in a back four, as there were situations where Palace had eight players forward with only the goalkeeper and two centre-backs staying back.

Coventry were far from convincing defensively but found a way to beat their relegation rivals, climbing to 13th on 12 points, three clear of the drop zone.

Tatsuhiro Sakamoto celebrates scoring Coventry's second with Jack Rudoni

Frank Lampard’s side have now won four of their last seven games and sit above fellow promoted sides Hull and Ipswich — an impressive feat after losing their first four games back in the Premier League.

The Coventry boss said: ‘It’s a big win for us. Every win for us in this league is a big win. But when a game is that tight, it’s important to get what we got.

‘After our start, where we played the best three teams in the league, we had zero points after four games, and now where we are is great progression.

‘That’s only down to hard work. We are the underdog in most games, so for them to experience and live difficult moments that this league will bring, it will help the players grow.’

#1549. AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone: Five things we learned – centrality and consistency

AC Milan put on a show at San Siro on Sunday night as they swept Frosinone aside emphatically, beating them 5-1.

The own-goal that Gabriele Calvani scored a few minutes in set the tone for the visitors, while Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. However, Patrizio Masini’s goal shortly after meant the deficit was halved going into the break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the second half, Milan ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both had opportunities after being found in behind, and both just minutes after coming off the bench. Then, Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

It was a win that Milan needed, considering that only Inter out of the current top six, dropped points, and it moves the Rossoneri back into the top four spots. Ivan Stoev has picked out the key talking points from the game.

Technically, Rabiot won the MOTM in our post-game ratings, but we absolutely have to talk about Luka Modric.

I’ve personally had my doubts about the Croatian being able to keep up this season, especially under Ruben Amorim. We all expected the Portuguese coach to bring a lot of intensity to Milan’s game and at times, Modric has seemed to struggle.

Maybe that was because of the team adapting to the new coach, or maybe the midfielder hadn’t completely recovered after the World Cup – who knows.

The reality is that the former Real Madrid man has stepped up after some shaky games at the start of the season and continues to prove his quality on and off the ball and his athleticism and longevity are nothing short of extraordinary.

The vision and passing ability to play the through ball to Rabiot for the opening goal was world-class. He then continued to dictate the tempo and make impressive forward runs, playing the full 90 minutes, giving it his all until the final whistle.

The management really needs to assemble a whole group of people tasked to find a proper replacement for Modric, as he will leave a big gap in that midfield.

To continue with the midfielder theme, we also have to give praise to Rabiot, who has been absolutely brilliant this season. Don’t get me wrong, he was one of the Rossoneri’s best players last year too.

Yet he has found a higher level since the start of the campaign, as he racked up another two assists and forced the own goal. As a result, he now has five goals and seven assists in 10 games in Serie A – extraordinary numbers.

On top of the goal contributions, you can count on the Frenchman to be composed under pressure, tidy with his passing, and efficient in both phases of the game. An absolutely stunning start of the season for Rabiot, who is finding new levels to his game under Amorim.

It was such a dominant win that we can probably cover each player and the positives from their game. Nevertheless, one man needs to be praised for sure and that’s Goncalo Ramos, who got himself back on the scoresheet.

Needless to say, he opened up a lot of spaces for his teammates and had a role in some of the other goals, which he was doing even when he failed to get the ball in the back of the net. This time around, he also got his long-awaited goal.

It was a beauty too, in the sense that he dropped deep into his own half, made the tackle to win the ball and kicked off the counter-attack. Following that, he made the run into the opponent’s box and finished it calmly – it was beautifully orchestrated with Ramos in the centre.

The goal and the encouraging performance are also a relief, as we’ve seen many times how strikers struggle to react when they are not scoring, with the confidence level often dropping which results in overall poor form.

However, the Portuguese striker is clearly not in his head and reacted well to a poor spell that spanned both his club and the national team, as he struggled in the international break too.

We didn’t even see that much of him as Amorim subbed him off rather early and it probably has to do with the fact that Milan need a win on Thursday against Olympiacos, in Greece, and Ramos will most likely start the game as the margin for error is little as things stand.

I mean, what more can you ask from your attackers? Diego Moreira got the hockey assist on the second goal and got an assist for Cisse in the second half and on top of that, was heavily involved and dangerous when the Diavolo went on the counter.

Truthfully, the Belgian should have probably scored a goal or two as he had some very good chances in the opponent’s penalty box, but his shooting let him down this time around. Nevertheless, another electric performance.

Speaking of electric – Pulisic also did very well as he was involved in the first goal – even if it ended up being an own goal, his run forced the Frosinone defender to run back and eventually put the ball in his own net.

The American then got his goal in the second half with a composed finish. He had a very solid game overall with lots of smart movements and combination play- nothing flashy, but the efficiency was there.

Then we also have Cisse, who started the game on the bench but only needed nine or so minutes after coming on to get his goal. Ridiculously, he now has six in 10 in the league or a goal every 74 minutes. The youngster made a good run and managed to keep himself onside in a tricky situation and then finished with composure.

The variety in attack by Milan on the night was a joy to watch, as all the players posed a threat to Frosinone, which in the end was too much for them to handle.

Amorim was well aware of how Frosinone would approach the game, which in itself deserves credit as they came to San Siro to play football instead of sitting back. Unfortunately for them and fortunately for us, the coach and his players knew exactly how to get around the high press.

The Rossoneri were rapid on the counter and created so many chances that the score could’ve easily been even worse for Frosinone. Their high press also didn’t work, as for the majority of the game the Diavolo managed to move the ball around quickly enough, which prevented their opponents from winning it in dangerous areas.

It also must be said that the Portuguese did well to rest some key players after the third goal, as he will need a fresh lineup for the Europa League fixture on Thursday, where Milan need three points against Olympiacos.

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

Also, it was Pulisics’ pass to Moreira that set-up Cisse’s goal. If were recognizing “hockey assists” then Pulisic’s pass to Moreira was also world-class. Not to be a wet-blanket, but Moreira and Cisse need to develop composure on the ball. Too often Moreira would negate his speed on the ball by dribbling into multiple defenders without looking to pass to an open teammate. Against the top teams Milan will not have as many goal scoring opportunities as they did on Sunday so now is the time to work on finding the open man in the final third.

So young players with potential, need to learn to be better and realise thier potential.

It was a pass in a 3v3 counter-attack situation. Great pass but Modric took out 5 defenders with 1 move. That is why it is world class and Pulisic pass is not mentioned as much.

Did anyone notice how Pulisic slowed down his run, thus letting Ramos reach the penalty box earlier and score his long awaited goal? Such a team player..

He’s always been that guy. Sometimes I wish he can be more ‘selfish’. Another example is the penalty fiasco with Tammy back then.

Yet some people here have called him selfish many times – especially last season when he wasn’t scoring. But then again, those same people praised Leao and probably thought he was Ballon d’Or material. LOL. 🤦‍♂️😂😂😂

Yes. I’d say it was as much about letting Ramos score as it was about “arriving” in the box late, setting up a cut back score, which he learned from Frank Lampard. Both are good things.

#1547. Big Decision From Manchester United Captain As Pochettino Is Set To Take Over

Manchester United transfer news: Red Devils captain Bruno Fernandes has turned down a second contract offer, according to a report from The Athletic covered by CaughtOffside. The 32-year-old is unhappy with both the proposed salary and the length of the deal, and the standoff lands with his current contract set to expire in June 2027.

The calendar adds pressure. In 50 days, Fernandes can open talks with foreign clubs, and Galatasaray have already been linked. United hold a 12-month extension option that stops him leaving for free, but triggering it only postpones the argument and keeps an unhappy captain in the dressing room.

The refusal follows a bad few weeks. After a 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes publicly criticised Michael Carrick’s tactics, and Carrick dropped him for the Bournemouth game. Carrick has since been sacked with United 18th in the Premier League, inside the relegation zone, so Mauricio Pochettino inherits the standoff alongside a team in trouble.

His strengths are obvious. He set a Premier League record with 21 assists last season, delivers set pieces better than anyone at the club and opened this campaign with a hat-trick against Ipswich. His weaknesses are just as clear. At 32, the Portuguese international gives little protection when United lose the ball, and his shot selection can be wasteful.

Pochettino’s best sides pressed hard and ran through a creative number ten with two athletic midfielders behind him. Fernandes suits the creative role, but only if those two midfielders cover his space.

United should keep him, but on shorter terms than he wants. Nobody else in the squad creates chances at his rate, and a team sitting in the bottom three cannot replace that in January. A long, expensive deal for a player entering his mid-thirties would create a wage problem just as Pochettino tries to rebuild the midfield around younger runners.

The sensible offer is a short contract with a raise tied to appearances and Champions League qualification. That respects his standing without committing United beyond the point where his legs start to fail.

If Fernandes still refuses, the board should trigger the extension and sell next summer. A sale with a year left on his deal will still bring a meaningful fee, whereas losing him for nothing in 2027 would waste the one asset United can sell on their own terms.

#1545. Arsenal, Liverpool, Chelsea Chase £100m England Midfielder

Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea have all contacted Bournemouth about England midfielder Alex Scott, according to CaughtOffside, which cites The i Paper. Liverpool and Chelsea want to move in January, while Arsenal would rather wait until next summer. Bournemouth’s stance on selling the 23-year-old has softened, but the reported asking price is above £100m, and Scott turned down two contract offers over the summer.

The interest has clear reasons behind it. Andoni Iraola coached Scott at Bournemouth before taking over at Anfield in June, and Liverpool want to reunite them. Chelsea lost Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City in a £125m deadline-day deal and had a reported £64m bid for Scott rejected earlier in the summer. Arsenal already have Declan Rice, Bruno Guimaraes, Martin Zubimendi and Myles Lewis-Skelly, so CaughtOffside sees Chelsea or Liverpool as the more logical destinations for his playing time.

Scott wins the ball, presses and carries it through midfield, and he started Bournemouth’s first five league games this season before a quadriceps injury on England duty in October kept him out for weeks. Fitness is the first concern, because knee problems have interrupted much of his time on the south coast. End product is the second. He has scored five league goals in 85 appearances since joining in 2023, so he will not solve a shortage of chances alone.

Not at £100m, and not as a January priority. Liverpool rank 18th for big chances after ten league games, according to This Is Anfield, and Scott offers energy rather than creativity. The real gap sits beside Ryan Gravenberch, where Curtis Jones left in the summer, and nobody arrived to share the defensive work.

Scott could be the aggressive partner in Iraola’s double pivot, freeing Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz to play higher, yet that is a heavy fee for a player only just rebuilding match fitness, with Liverpool fourth and nine points behind Arsenal.

Chelsea’s case is simpler. The division’s biggest summer spenders lost their midfield engine and can justify the price more easily. Arsenal’s patience makes sense, since Rice, Guimaraes and Zubimendi leave no room for a £100m squad player. A Liverpool bid would only inflate the market Chelsea are already shaping. #1544. Aston Villa news: Why Unai Emery's immunity from criticism should no longer exist

By Darren Plant | 25 Nov 2026 12:36

Such is Unai Emery's status at Aston Villa that few would be surprised if the redeveloped North Stand, when completed in 2027, is named after the Spaniard.

Taking Villa from relegation candidates in 2022-23 to two Champions League qualifications and a Europa League trophy by the conclusion of 2025-26 arguably deserves that level of recognition.

However, despite the expectation that a contract extension past 2029 will be penned in the near future, it will not necessarily strengthen Emery's, or the club's, position in the long term.

Tuesday's 1-0 defeat at Galatasaray extended Villa's recent winless streak across all competitions to six matches. They have failed to score in four of those games, and given up leads on three occasions.

Emery is no stranger to an extended blip in form. At the start of both 2025-26 and 2026-27, Villa were off the pace. It is to Emery's credit that Villa became brief Premier League title contenders in a matter of months and still finished in fourth position in last season's standings.

Nevertheless, Villa are now enduring their second extended winless period of the season, raising the question of whether the West Midlands outfit are experiencing a blip or a gradual decline under their most successful manager for nearly 45 years?

With 116 wins from 215 matches, silverware, and delivering moments and experiences that will last a lifetime, Emery is etched into the Villa history books as a God.

At the same time, this is now a manager of a team that has only recorded 11 wins from his last 27 games in all competitions, as well as losing on 10 occasions. Just seven wins have come from 19 fixtures in 2026-27.

When Villa defeated Tottenham Hotspur, Newcastle United and Manchester City in relatively quick succession with performances that mixed grit, shrewdness and attacking vigour, the conclusion was that Emery's new-looked team had flicked a switch.

However, Villa have regressed as quickly as they had seemingly improved. When you take into account that Villa had one win in seven between February 1 and March 4, and lost three in a row between April 25 and May 3, this is now the fourth "blip" in less than nine months.

Some of the aforementioned statistics will be comparable with managers at similarly-sized clubs in the Premier League and Europe, yet that usually leads to scrutiny over the job that has been conducted over a specific period. Not talk of a contract until 2030 and beyond being signed.

By modern-day standards, Emery is in the unique position of having high control over which players are signed and sold. He essentially has the keys to the footballing side of the club and Villa's fate on the pitch is solely in his hands.

Yet, a 12-time trophy-winning manager of a team that has only earned fewer Premier League points than Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool across a four-year period is frequently telling the media, or anyone who will listen, that Villa should not be competing in the top six, nor for the top-eight positions in the league phase of the Champions League.

Is this an example of Emery trying to reinforce the perception that Villa are underdogs to the so-called Premier League 'big six' because of what is, admittedly, a scandalous PSR scenario, or is it a pre-orchestrated approach to defend his position whenever results do not go Villa's way?

Staying on the subject of things being pre-orchestrated, not enough scrutiny is coming over Villa's and Emery's use of Liverpool's Harvey Elliott and Chelsea's Alejandro Garnacho.

Since the summer of 2025, Villa have included £35m and, allegedly, £43m fees with those clubs to sign the players in question should they achieve a specific appearance threshold. Between them, they have made three starts and 13 substitute outings when spending the majority of the time available for selection.

On Tuesday night, Emery omitted Garnacho - who has accumulated fewer than 100 minutes across seven substitute appearances - from the squad for the Galatasaray match, despite naming one fewer substitute than was permitted. Afterwards, he delivered a frank response over the Argentine's chances of earning future game time.

If Villa do not want to pay vast amounts of money for players, they do not have to. However, are Villa not harming their chances of signing players through similar deals in the future? Why should clubs trust such deals to go through if Emery is choosing not to select such players or is being told not to?

Everything points to Garnacho becoming Elliott 2:0 and the situation deserves some clarity. If an honest assessment cannot be delivered to fans and the media, Emery leaves himself open to persistent questioning and criticism, and it will be warranted.

Of course, the evolving Garnacho saga can change for the better. Excluding Villa's game against Chelsea in December, the winger has seven more chances to feature in 2026.

There can be a rapid upturn in fortunes, too. Villa face Ipswich Town, Everton and Crystal Palace in the Premier League before they welcome Paris Saint-Germain to Villa Park in the Champions League.

However, when Emery is storming down tunnels before the full-time whistle, throwing tantrums in the media and getting increasingly frustrated on the touchline as his team look slow, devoid of ideas and can make 700 passes in a game and not score against a team such as Sunderland, it can be argued that Villa need a change of direction rather than remaining on their current path.

Villa have a deep squad with talent that can earn them success in the future, yet they have too many under-performers or players who may simply be tired even at this stage of the season. Whether that is down to Emery, or too much emphasis being placed on players needing to adapt to the "Emery way" before they earn regular starts, it is open to debate.

Regardless, Villa are currently on a downward trajectory under his leadership, and Emery has questions to answer if he is to remain untouchable at a club that want to hand him a contract extension when they could enter December with just three Premier League wins in 2026-27.

Liverpool transfer news: Ryan Gravenberch’s agent, José Fortes Rodriguez, is exploring ways to take his client out of Anfield, according to CaughtOffside. The site relays a claim from the X account @ITKSpace that Fortes has held “loose but direct contact” with several European clubs, none of them named. No formal exit request has been lodged, and the 24-year-old could still stay, so this reads like a camp checking the market rather than a player pushing to leave.

Liverpool hold the stronger hand. His six-year extension, signed in March, runs to 2032, so any buyer would face a substantial asking price. Real Madrid have been linked before, though nothing here says they are interested now.

Iraola’s 4-2-3-1 relies on two central midfielders, and Gravenberch, so commanding at the base of Arne Slot’s title-winning side, has struggled to settle. Iraola benched him for three straight games at one stage, he collected a second yellow card in the 3-0 home defeat by Manchester City on 11 October, and a heel problem has since kept him out of the Arsenal and Fenerbahçe games. He has no goals and one assist in the league this term.

His strengths are clear. At 6ft 3in he carries the ball through pressure and starts attacks from deep. Defending space and tracking runners is the weakness, and it shows when his partner also surges forward.

No, not this winter and not at a price set by his worst few weeks. Gravenberch is 24, tied down until 2032, and his market value has slipped sharply since last December, so selling now would hand a buyer the bargain that March contract was meant to rule out.

The real problem sits elsewhere. Iraola received no new midfielder in the summer, and his double pivot has no natural holding player. Gravenberch has admitted he prefers the number eight role, yet Mac Allister and Szoboszlai, who started the 3-1 win at Crystal Palace that lifted Liverpool to fourth, already occupy those spots. Nineteen-year-old Trey Nyoni has mostly played the deeper role this season.

Keep him through January, get him fit, and judge him again in a settled pairing. If Liverpool then sign a proper holding midfielder next summer, Gravenberch becomes a surplus eight, and a big-club bid at the right figure would deserve a hearing. Selling before that signing arrives just removes the one midfielder who can still carry the ball out of pressure.

#1542. Villa Midfielder Has £80m Price Tag For Arsenal: Is He Worth It?

Arsenal transfer news: Aston Villa do not regard Boubacar Kamara as available, even with Arsenal interested, according to CaughtOffside. The report says an offer of around £80m could change that stance, although Villa negotiate from strength because the 26-year-old’s contract runs until 2030.

January looks highly unlikely. Villa have already lost Amadou Onana to a torn ACL suffered at the World Cup, and the Belgian is not expected back until around April. Unai Emery cannot lose a second holding midfielder in the middle of a season. The summer is different. CaughtOffside says Villa could entertain a significant bid then, provided they can reinvest the money in a proper replacement and strengthen the squad around him.

TBR Football reported in July 2025 that he sat on Arsenal’s long list of midfield targets, and his numbers explain why. Kamara has started all 10 of his Premier League games this season, completing 86.3% of his passes, including 83 line-breaking balls, while making 28 tackles and 40 recoveries. He wins 56% of his duels and can play at centre-back, which would give Mikel Arteta cover in two positions.

The weaknesses are just as clear. He has no goals this season, only three shots and an xG of 0.14, and he has committed 20 fouls and conceded a penalty. He also missed the closing weeks of 2024/25 through injury.

The role he would play is obvious: a ball-playing six next to Declan Rice. Martín Zubimendi occupies it now, and Arsenal lead the league with 27 points from 10 games, six clear of Manchester City, with seven clean sheets.

No, not at that price. Arsenal spent £75m on Bruno Guimarães in August, and Arteta still has Rice, Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Martin Ødegaard and Myles Lewis-Skelly competing for the same central spaces.

FotMob values him at €49m, roughly £43m, so Villa would be asking close to double his market value for a player who turns 27 this month and offers little in the final third. Villa’s insistence on reinvesting the fee also hands them the leverage, which means Arsenal would pay a premium on a seller’s timetable.

The only sensible trigger is a departure, perhaps Zubimendi or the 30-year-old Merino, leaving Arsenal short of a proven Premier League six. Kamara is a better holding midfielder than most of the market, but a title-leading side already has that job covered, and £80m would buy cover rather than improvement.
